A DC motor with V = 220 V, Ia = 20 A and Ra = 0.5 ohm has a back EMF of:
The speed of a DC motor is proportional to:
mcq.e: Since Eb is proportional to phi N, N is proportional to Eb/phi.

mcq.q: A DC machine operates at maximum efficiency when:
o: Copper loss is twice the iron loss
mcq.e: Differentiating efficiency with respect to current gives Ia^2 Ra = constant losses.

mcq.q: Swinburne's test is NOT suitable for DC series motors because:
o: They cannot be run safely at no load
mcq.e: The test needs no-load running, at which a series motor would overspeed dangerously.

mcq.q: The short circuit test on a transformer gives:
o: Full-load copper loss and equivalent impedance
mcq.e: At reduced voltage with rated current, input power is essentially copper loss.
mcq.t: Open circuit and short circuit tests

mcq.q: All-day efficiency of a distribution transformer is the ratio of:
o: Output power to input power at full load
Output kWh to input kWh over 24 hours
mcq.e: It is an energy efficiency because load varies through the day.

mcq.q: A transformer's full-load copper loss is 400 W. Its copper loss at half load is:
mcq.e: Copper loss varies as the square of load: 400 x (1/2)^2 = 100 W.

mcq.q: Which condition is essential (not merely desirable) for parallel operation of single-phase transformers?
mcq.e: Wrong polarity creates a short circuit through the secondaries; other conditions affect load sharing.

mcq.q: An autotransformer differs from a two-winding transformer in that it has:
o: A single winding, part of which is common to both circuits
mcq.e: Primary and secondary share a common winding, so they are not electrically isolated.

mcq.q: The Scott connection is used to convert:
mcq.e: Two single-phase transformers (main and teaser) give a balanced two-phase output.

mcq.q: In a Scott connection, the teaser transformer primary has how many turns compared with the main transformer primary?
mcq.e: The teaser primary needs sqrt(3)/2 of the main's turns to give equal secondary voltages.

mcq.q: In a delta-star transformer, the secondary line voltage is displaced from the primary line voltage by:
mcq.e: Dyn11 and similar delta-star groups introduce a 30 degree phase shift.

mcq.q: Skin effect in a conductor carrying AC causes its effective resistance to:
mcq.e: Current crowds to the surface, reducing effective area and raising resistance.

mcq.e: r' = r e^(-1/4) = 0.7788r accounts for internal flux linkage.

mcq.q: In a string of suspension insulators, the maximum voltage appears across the disc:
mcq.e: Shunt capacitance to earth makes the disc nearest the conductor carry the most voltage.

mcq.q: A guard ring fitted to an insulator string is used to:
mcq.e: It equalises voltage distribution across discs, raising string efficiency.

mcq.q: Span 200 m, conductor weight 10 N/m and tension 20000 N with level supports. The sag is:
Pin-type insulators are generally economical only up to about:
mcq.e: Above about 33 kV pin insulators become too bulky, so suspension types are used.

mcq.q: In a single-core cable, the maximum electric stress occurs at:
mcq.e: Stress varies as 1/x, so it is highest at the conductor surface.

mcq.q: Grading of cables is done to:
mcq.e: Grading distributes stress more evenly across the insulation.

mcq.q: The insulation resistance of a cable is:
mcq.e: R = (ρ/2πl) ln(R/r), so longer cables have lower insulation resistance.

mcq.q: For minimum stress at the conductor for a fixed sheath diameter D, the ratio D/d should be:
mcq.e: Minimising gmax gives ln(D/d) = 1, so D/d = e.

mcq.q: Kelvin's law gives the most economical size of conductor when the annual cost of energy lost equals the:
o: Annual interest and depreciation on conductor capital cost
mcq.e: Kelvin's law equates variable capital charges to annual energy-loss cost.

mcq.q: Which of the following is a FACTS device?
mcq.e: STATCOM is a shunt FACTS controller for reactive power.

mcq.q: An advantage of HVDC transmission over HVAC is the absence of:
o: Line charging current and reactive power flow
mcq.e: DC lines carry no charging current or reactive power in steady state.

mcq.q: Compared with a radial distributor, a ring main distributor offers:
mcq.e: Consumers can be fed from either side, so a fault causes fewer interruptions.

mcq.e: HF dissolves SiO2 selectively during oxide etching.

mcq.q: In IC fabrication, silicon dioxide is used mainly as:

mcq.q: In monolithic bipolar ICs, components are commonly isolated by:

mcq.q: Voltage-shunt feedback in an op-amp forms which amplifier?

mcq.q: The input impedance of an ideal op-amp is:

mcq.q: Roll-off rate of a first-order active low-pass filter beyond cutoff is:

mcq.q: An astable multivibrator has how many stable states?

mcq.q: A clamper circuit:

mcq.q: A second-order Butterworth low-pass filter rolls off at:

mcq.q: How many pins does the standard IC 555 timer DIP package have?

mcq.q: In PWM using a 555 monostable, the modulating signal is applied to:

mcq.q: The AD633 output (W, with Z grounded) is:

mcq.q: The LM7805 regulator gives an output of:

mcq.q: The ICL8038 function generator can produce which waveforms simultaneously?
mcq.e: ICL8038 provides sine, square and triangle outputs.

mcq.q: The closeness of a measured value to the true value is called:
mcq.e: Accuracy is closeness to the true value.

mcq.q: The smallest change in input that an instrument can detect is its:
mcq.e: Resolution is the smallest detectable input increment.

mcq.q: Errors due to incorrect reading of instruments by the observer are:
mcq.e: Human mistakes in reading or recording are gross errors.

mcq.q: For a normal distribution, about what percent of readings lie within ±1 standard deviation?
mcq.e: About 68.3% of normally distributed data lies within ±1σ.

mcq.q: PMMC instruments can be used to measure:
mcq.e: PMMC deflection reverses with current, so it measures DC only.

mcq.q: The scale of a moving iron instrument is:
mcq.e: Deflecting torque ∝ I^2, giving a non-uniform scale.

mcq.q: A megger is used to measure:
mcq.e: A megger measures high insulation resistance.

mcq.q: The secondary of a CT should never be:
mcq.e: An open CT secondary develops dangerously high voltage and core saturation.

mcq.q: At balance of a Wheatstone bridge, P/Q =
mcq.e: At balance, P/Q = R/S and galvanometer current is zero.

mcq.q: Kelvin double bridge is used to measure:
mcq.e: Kelvin double bridge eliminates lead and contact resistance for low resistances.

mcq.q: Schering bridge is used to measure:
mcq.e: Schering bridge measures capacitance and loss angle of insulators.

mcq.q: Wien bridge is commonly used for measurement of:
mcq.e: Wien bridge balance depends on frequency, so it measures frequency.

mcq.q: A thermocouple is an example of a/an:
mcq.e: A thermocouple generates its own emf, so it is active.

mcq.q: LVDT is used to measure:
mcq.e: Linear Variable Differential Transformer measures linear displacement.

mcq.q: Gauge factor of a strain gauge is defined as:
mcq.e: Gauge factor = fractional change in resistance per unit strain.

mcq.q: An RTD measures temperature using change in:
mcq.e: Resistance of metals like platinum varies with temperature.

mcq.q: The fastest type of ADC is the:
mcq.e: Flash ADCs convert in one step using parallel comparators.

mcq.q: Resolution of an 8-bit ADC with 5.12 V full scale is about:
Number of comparators needed in an n-bit flash ADC is:
mcq.e: A flash ADC needs 2^n - 1 comparators.

mcq.q: LabVIEW programs are called:
mcq.e: Programs in LabVIEW are virtual instruments (VIs).

mcq.q: The 8085 microprocessor has a data bus width of:
mcq.e: 8085 is an 8-bit processor.

mcq.q: The 8085 can address a maximum memory of:
mcq.e: 16 address lines give 2^16 = 64 KB.

mcq.q: The non-maskable interrupt of 8085 is:
mcq.e: TRAP is non-maskable with highest priority.

mcq.q: In 8085, the lower order address and data lines are multiplexed and demultiplexed using the signal:
mcq.e: ALE latches the low-order address from AD0-AD7.

mcq.q: MVI A, 32H uses which addressing mode?
mcq.e: The data 32H is part of the instruction.

mcq.q: The instruction LDA 2050H is how many bytes long?
mcq.e: Opcode plus 16-bit address = 3 bytes.

mcq.q: When PUSH B is executed in 8085, the stack pointer:
mcq.e: Two bytes are stored, SP decrements by 2.

mcq.q: After MVI A, 0FFH followed by INR A, the zero flag and A are:
mcq.e: FFH + 1 wraps to 00H, setting Z; INR does not affect CY.

mcq.q: The 8255 PPI has how many 8-bit I/O ports?
mcq.e: 8255 has ports A, B and C.

mcq.q: The 8254 programmable timer contains how many 16-bit counters?
mcq.e: 8254 has three independent 16-bit counters.

mcq.q: The 8279 is a:
mcq.e: 8279 is a programmable keyboard and display interface.

mcq.q: An 8-bit DAC with 5 V full scale has a resolution of about:
The 8051 microcontroller has on-chip ROM of:
mcq.e: Standard 8051 has 4 KB on-chip program ROM.

mcq.q: The on-chip RAM of the 8051 is:
mcq.e: The basic 8051 has 128 bytes of internal RAM.

mcq.q: In 8051 timer mode 2, the timer operates as:
mcq.e: Mode 2 is 8-bit auto-reload, used for baud rate generation.

mcq.q: The number of I/O ports in 8051 is:
mcq.e: 8051 has four 8-bit ports P0-P3.

mcq.q: PIC microcontrollers use which architecture?
mcq.e: PIC has separate program and data memory buses.

mcq.q: The PIC16 mid-range family has approximately how many instructions?
mcq.e: PIC16 mid-range devices have 35 instructions.

mcq.q: RISC architecture is characterized by:
mcq.e: RISC uses a reduced set of simple instructions.

mcq.q: In PIC16 devices, data memory is divided into:
mcq.e: PIC16 RAM is organized in banks selected by STATUS register bits.

mcq.e: Low-speed hydro turbines use salient pole rotors with many poles.

mcq.q: Synchronous speed in rpm is given by Ns = :
mcq.e: Ns = 120f/P.

mcq.q: The EMF method of finding voltage regulation is also called the:
mcq.e: The synchronous impedance (EMF) method gives a higher (pessimistic) regulation value.

mcq.q: The slip test is used to determine:
mcq.e: The slip test measures direct and quadrature axis reactances.

mcq.q: A synchronous motor is not self-starting because:
o: The supply frequency is too low
The average torque on the rotor is zero at standstill
mcq.e: The rotating field alternately pulls the rotor both ways, giving zero average torque.

mcq.q: An over-excited synchronous motor operates at:
mcq.e: Over-excitation makes the motor draw leading current.

mcq.q: A synchronous motor running at no load and over-excited to improve power factor is called a:
mcq.e: It acts like a capacitor and is called a synchronous condenser.

mcq.q: Damper windings in a synchronous motor help to:
mcq.e: Damper windings damp oscillations and allow induction starting.

mcq.q: Slip of an induction motor is defined as:
mcq.e: s = (Ns - N)/Ns.

mcq.q: A 4-pole, 50 Hz induction motor runs at 1440 rpm. The slip is:
Maximum torque in an induction motor occurs when slip equals:
mcq.e: Maximum torque occurs at s = R2/X2.

mcq.q: Rotor copper loss in an induction motor equals:
mcq.e: Rotor copper loss = s × Pag.

mcq.q: In a star-delta starter, the starting current drawn from the line is reduced to:
mcq.e: Star-delta reduces starting line current and torque to one-third of DOL values.

mcq.q: Rotor resistance starters can be used only with:
mcq.e: External resistance can be added only through slip rings.

mcq.q: Braking by reversing two supply phases of an induction motor is:
mcq.e: Plugging reverses the phase sequence to produce reverse torque.

mcq.q: In V/f control, the ratio V/f is kept constant to keep constant:
mcq.e: Constant V/f maintains constant air-gap flux.

mcq.q: Double field revolving theory explains that a pulsating field can be resolved into:
o: Two rotating fields of half magnitude in opposite directions
mcq.e: A pulsating field equals two counter-rotating fields of half amplitude.

mcq.q: A shaded pole motor has starting torque that is:
mcq.e: Shaded pole motors have low starting torque.

mcq.q: A stepper motor with step angle 1.8° completes one revolution in:
mcq.e: Steps per revolution = 360/1.8 = 200.

mcq.q: The motor commonly used in electric clocks needing constant speed and self-starting is the:
mcq.e: Hysteresis motors run smoothly at synchronous speed and are used in clocks.

mcq.q: The diagonal element Yii of the bus admittance matrix equals:
o: Negative of admittance between buses i and j
Impedance of bus i to ground
Sum of all admittances connected to bus i
mcq.e: Yii is the self-admittance, the sum of all admittances terminating at bus i.

mcq.q: The base impedance for a base of 100 MVA and 11 kV is:
mcq.e: Zbase = kV²/MVA = 121/100 = 1.21 Ω.

mcq.q: Using the bus incidence matrix A and primitive admittance matrix y, Ybus is obtained as:
mcq.e: By singular transformation, Ybus = A^T [y] A.

mcq.q: For the slack (swing) bus, the specified quantities are:
mcq.e: The slack bus has fixed voltage magnitude and angle and supplies the system losses.

mcq.q: For a generator (PV) bus, the specified quantities are:
mcq.e: A PV bus has specified real power and voltage magnitude.

mcq.q: In Gauss-Seidel load flow, an acceleration factor is used to:
mcq.e: An acceleration factor (about 1.6) speeds up convergence of the Gauss-Seidel iterations.

mcq.q: The Newton-Raphson load flow method has a convergence characteristic that is:
mcq.e: NR converges quadratically near the solution, requiring far fewer iterations than Gauss-Seidel.

mcq.q: Which of the following is a symmetrical fault?
mcq.e: A balanced three-phase fault keeps the system symmetrical.

mcq.q: Current limiting reactors are used in power systems to:
mcq.e: Series reactors add impedance that restricts fault current to safe levels.

mcq.q: With a base of 100 MVA, the Thevenin impedance at a bus is 0.2 pu. The three-phase fault level is:
mcq.e: Fault MVA = base MVA / Zth(pu) = 100/0.2 = 500 MVA.

mcq.q: For a three-phase fault at bus k through impedance Zf, the fault current using Zbus is:
mcq.e: The Thevenin impedance at bus k is the diagonal element Zkk, so If = Vf/(Zkk + Zf).

mcq.q: For the operator a = 1∠120°, the value of 1 + a + a^2 is:
mcq.e: The three unit phasors spaced 120° apart sum to zero.

mcq.q: For a bolted LG fault at an unloaded generator, the positive-sequence current Ia1 is:
mcq.e: For an LG fault Ia1 = Ia2 = Ia0 = Ea/(Z1 + Z2 + Z0); the fault current is 3 times this.

mcq.q: For a line-to-line fault (not involving ground), the sequence networks are connected as:

mcq.e: An LL fault has no zero-sequence current, and the positive and negative networks are connected in parallel.

mcq.q: For a single line-to-ground fault, the three sequence networks are connected in:
o: Positive and negative in parallel only
mcq.e: The LG fault condition Ia1 = Ia2 = Ia0 is satisfied by connecting the sequence networks in series.

mcq.e: M d²δ/dt² = Pm - Pe; the net accelerating power drives rotor angle changes.

An RC snubber across a switch is used mainly to limit:

mcq.q: Output voltage of a single phase half bridge inverter with DC input Vdc is a square wave of amplitude:

mcq.q: In sinusoidal PWM, the modulation index is the ratio of:

mcq.q: In a current source inverter, the DC link contains a large:

mcq.q: A single phase full-wave bridge rectifier uses how many diodes?
mcq.e: Four diodes form the bridge.

mcq.q: Average output of a single phase full wave rectifier with peak Vm is:

mcq.q: A voltage doubler circuit produces a DC output of about:

mcq.q: The average output of a three phase diode bridge with line peak VmL is:

mcq.q: An SCR has how many PN junctions?

mcq.q: Average output of a single phase full converter with firing angle α is:
mcq.e: For continuous conduction, Vdc = (2Vm/π) cos α.

mcq.q: A full converter operates in inversion mode when firing angle α is:
mcq.e: cos α is negative beyond 90°, reversing average voltage.

mcq.q: A TRIAC is equivalent to:

mcq.e: A TRIAC conducts in both directions like two inverse-parallel SCRs.

mcq.q: A TRIAC can be triggered by:

mcq.e: TRIACs can be turned on with either gate polarity.

mcq.q: AC voltage controllers using phase control change the:
mcq.e: Phase control varies the RMS output at the same frequency.

mcq.q: In a single phase AC voltage controller with resistive load, increasing firing angle:
mcq.e: A later firing angle reduces the conducting portion of each half cycle.

mcq.q: The distinguishing feature of a closed-loop control system is:
mcq.e: Closed-loop systems compare the fed-back output with the reference input.

mcq.q: A transfer function is defined assuming:
mcq.e: TF = Laplace of output / Laplace of input with all initial conditions zero.

mcq.q: The closed-loop transfer function with forward path G and negative feedback H is:
mcq.e: Reducing a negative feedback loop gives C/R = G/(1 + GH).

mcq.q: In the force-voltage analogy, mass is analogous to:
mcq.e: F = M dv/dt corresponds to v = L di/dt, so M maps to L.

mcq.q: A second-order system with damping ratio zeta = 0 is:
mcq.e: With zero damping the response oscillates with constant amplitude.

mcq.q: For a unit step input, the steady-state error of a type-1 system is:
mcq.e: Type-1 systems have infinite Kp, so step error 1/(1 + Kp) is zero.

mcq.q: A second-order system has wn = 10 rad/s and zeta = 0.5. Its 2% settling time is:
In the Routh array, the number of sign changes in the first column equals the number of:
o: Roots in the right half s-plane
mcq.e: Each sign change in the first column indicates one right-half-plane root.

mcq.q: Gain margin is the reciprocal of the open-loop magnitude at the:
mcq.e: At the phase crossover (phase = -180 degrees), GM = 1/|G(jw)H(jw)|.

mcq.q: In a Bode magnitude plot, a simple pole at the origin contributes a slope of:
mcq.e: 1/(jw) has magnitude falling by 20 dB for each decade of frequency.

mcq.q: A lead compensator mainly:
o: Adds phase lead and improves transient response
Adds phase lag at all frequencies
mcq.e: Positive phase near crossover raises phase margin and speeds the response.

mcq.q: For a standard second-order system, a resonant peak (Mr > 1) occurs only when zeta is less than:
mcq.e: Mr = 1/(2 zeta sqrt(1 - zeta^2)) exists for zeta < 1/sqrt(2).

mcq.q: The eigenvalues of the system matrix A are the system's:
mcq.e: Roots of |sI - A| = 0 are the characteristic roots, i.e. the poles.

mcq.q: The state transition matrix of x' = A x is:
mcq.e: phi(t) = e^(At) = inverse Laplace of (sI - A)^-1.

mcq.q: By Kalman's test, an nth-order system is controllable if the rank of [B AB ... A^(n-1)B] is:
mcq.e: Full rank n of the controllability matrix ensures all states can be driven.

mcq.q: The eigenvalues of A = [[0, 1], [-2, -3]] are:
mcq.e: Characteristic equation s^2 + 3s + 2 = 0 gives s = -1 and s = -2.

mcq.q: Which control action eliminates steady-state error for a step input?
mcq.e: Integral action accumulates error and adds a pole at the origin.

mcq.q: In the Ziegler-Nichols ultimate gain method, the proportional gain for a PID controller is:
mcq.e: Z-N PID settings are Kp = 0.6 Ku, Ti = 0.5 Pu, Td = 0.125 Pu.

mcq.q: A lag compensator is mainly used to:
mcq.e: It raises low-frequency gain, reducing steady-state error, with little effect on transient response.

mcq.q: In the transfer function of a lead compensator (s + z)/(s + p):
o: The pole is closer to the origin than the zero
The zero is closer to the origin than the pole
Both lie in the right half plane
mcq.e: z < p makes the zero dominate first, giving positive phase.

mcq.q: The most frequently occurring fault in power systems is:
mcq.e: About 70-80% of faults are single line-to-ground.

mcq.q: Which fault is generally the most severe?
mcq.e: The three-phase symmetrical fault usually gives the highest fault current.

mcq.q: Adjacent protective zones are overlapped so that:
o: No part of the system is left unprotected
mcq.e: Overlapping prevents blind spots between zones.

mcq.q: For resonant (Peterson coil) grounding, the coil reactance XL is chosen equal to:
mcq.e: XL = 1/(3ωC) makes the coil current cancel the capacitive fault current.

mcq.q: On the R-X diagram, the characteristic of a plain impedance relay is:
o: A circle centred at the origin
A circle passing through the origin
mcq.e: It operates when |Z| is below a set value, a circle about the origin.

mcq.q: A differential relay operates on the:
o: Difference between currents entering and leaving a zone
mcq.e: It trips when the vector difference of currents exceeds a setting.

mcq.q: The characteristic of a mho relay on the R-X diagram is a:
o: Straight line parallel to R axis
mcq.e: The mho relay is inherently directional with a circle through the origin.

mcq.q: Under-frequency relays are mainly used for:
mcq.e: They shed load when frequency falls due to generation deficit.

mcq.q: The secondary of a current transformer must never be open-circuited while energised because:
mcq.e: With no secondary ampere-turns the core saturates and very high voltage appears.

mcq.q: A Buchholz relay is used to protect:
mcq.e: It senses gas and oil surge from internal faults in transformers.

mcq.q: Merz-Price circulating current protection is commonly used for:
mcq.e: It is a differential scheme widely applied to generator windings.

mcq.q: Transformer differential relays use harmonic restraint because magnetising inrush current is rich in the:
mcq.e: Inrush has a large second harmonic, used to block false tripping.

mcq.q: Static relays differ from electromagnetic relays mainly in that they:
o: Use solid-state circuits with no moving parts for measurement
mcq.e: Measurement is performed by electronic circuits instead of moving elements.

mcq.q: In a numerical relay, the analog CT/VT signals are converted to digital by:
mcq.e: Signals are filtered, sampled and digitised by an ADC.

mcq.q: An anti-aliasing low-pass filter in a numerical relay is placed:
o: Before the sampling and A/D conversion
mcq.e: It removes frequencies above half the sampling rate before sampling.

mcq.q: An amplitude comparator with inputs S1 and S2 can be converted into a phase comparator by using inputs:
mcq.e: Amplitude and phase comparators are duals via sum and difference inputs.

mcq.q: SF6 gas is used in circuit breakers because it is:
mcq.e: SF6 captures free electrons, giving high dielectric strength and fast recovery.

mcq.q: Current chopping in a circuit breaker produces:
mcq.e: Abrupt current interruption releases inductive energy as high voltage.

mcq.q: The rate of rise of restriking voltage (RRRV) is usually expressed in:
mcq.e: RRRV is the slope of the restriking voltage, typically in kV/μs.
mcq.t: Rate of rise of recovery voltage

mcq.q: Resistance switching in circuit breakers is used to:
mcq.e: A shunt resistor damps the transient and reduces RRRV.

mcq.q: What is the nominal frequency of the Indian power grid?
mcq.e: India operates its grid at 50 Hz.

mcq.q: Load factor is defined as:
mcq.e: Load factor = average demand / maximum demand.

mcq.q: Real power in a power system is closely coupled with:
mcq.e: P-f and Q-V loops are largely decoupled; real power governs frequency.

mcq.q: A system with average load 60 MW and peak load 100 MW has load factor:
mcq.e: Load factor = 60/100 = 0.6.

mcq.q: Speed regulation (droop) R of a governor is expressed as:
o: Change in frequency per unit change in power
Change in power per unit frequency
mcq.e: R = Δf/ΔP.

mcq.q: With integral control in a single-area LFC, the steady-state frequency error after a step load is:
mcq.e: Integral action eliminates steady-state frequency error.

mcq.q: A single-area system (R = 0.05 pu, no load damping, 50 Hz) sees a 0.1 pu load rise. Steady Δf is:
Area Control Error (ACE) for a two-area system is:
mcq.e: ACE combines tie-line power deviation and frequency bias times Δf.

mcq.q: An AVR controls generator terminal voltage by adjusting:
mcq.e: The AVR varies field current to regulate voltage.

mcq.q: Shunt capacitors connected at a bus:
o: Supply reactive power and raise voltage
mcq.e: Capacitors generate VArs, boosting bus voltage.

mcq.q: An over-excited synchronous condenser:
mcq.e: Over-excitation makes it behave like a capacitor, supplying VArs.
mcq.t: Generation and absorption of reactive power

mcq.q: The approximate voltage drop in a short line delivering P and Q is:
mcq.e: ΔV ≈ (PR + QX)/V.

mcq.q: Neglecting losses, economic dispatch requires all units to operate at:
mcq.e: Optimality condition: dCi/dPi = λ for all units.

mcq.q: IC1 = 0.1P1 + 20 and IC2 = 0.1P2 + 16 (Rs/MWh). For 140 MW demand (no losses), P1 is:
mcq.e: Equal IC gives P2 = P1 + 40 and P1 + P2 = 140, so P1 = 50 MW.

mcq.q: With transmission losses, the penalty factor of unit i is:
mcq.e: Li = 1/(1 - ∂PL/∂Pi) scales each unit's incremental cost.

mcq.q: The unit of incremental fuel cost is:
mcq.e: Incremental cost dC/dP has units of cost per energy, e.g. Rs/MWh.

mcq.q: SCADA stands for:
mcq.e: SCADA = Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition.

mcq.q: PMUs time-stamp synchrophasor measurements using:
mcq.e: PMUs synchronise to GPS to give a common time reference.

mcq.q: In WLS state estimation, the weight for each measurement is usually:
mcq.e: More accurate meters (smaller variance) get larger weights 1/σ^2.

mcq.q: Which is NOT one of the power system operating states in the Dy Liacco classification?
mcq.e: The states are normal, alert, emergency, in extremis and restorative.

mcq.q: The standard lightning impulse voltage waveform is:
mcq.e: Standard lightning impulse is 1.2 μs front and 50 μs tail.

mcq.q: Standard switching impulse waveform is:
mcq.e: Switching impulse standard is 250/2500 μs.

mcq.q: For a travelling wave reaching an open-circuited line end, the voltage reflection coefficient is:
mcq.e: Open end: Z = ∞ gives reflection coefficient +1, doubling voltage.

mcq.q: A line of surge impedance Z0 is terminated in Z0. The reflected voltage is:
mcq.e: Matched termination gives zero reflection.

mcq.q: Paschen's law relates breakdown voltage to the product of:
mcq.e: Breakdown voltage V = f(pd).

mcq.q: SF6 is widely used in HV equipment because it is:
mcq.e: SF6 attaches electrons, giving high dielectric strength and arc quenching.

mcq.q: Townsend's first ionization coefficient α represents:
o: Electrons released per incident positive ion
Ionizing collisions per electron per unit length
mcq.e: α is the number of ionizing collisions made by an electron per cm in the field direction.

mcq.q: Breakdown in solid dielectrics occurring in about 10^-8 s with no thermal effects is:
mcq.e: Intrinsic breakdown is very fast and depends only on the material and field.

mcq.q: Cockcroft-Walton circuit is used to generate:
mcq.e: It is a voltage multiplier using diodes and capacitors to give high DC.

mcq.q: Marx circuit is used to generate:
mcq.e: Marx generator charges capacitors in parallel and discharges in series for impulses.

mcq.q: Cascaded transformers are used to generate:
mcq.e: Cascading transformer units produces very high AC test voltages.

mcq.q: The sphere gap is used for measuring:
o: Peak values of AC, DC and impulse voltages
mcq.e: Sphere gaps measure peak voltages of DC, AC and impulse.

mcq.q: Testing standards in India are issued by:
mcq.e: The Bureau of Indian Standards publishes Indian testing standards.

mcq.q: A test that must be withstood without damage to prove insulation level is a:
mcq.e: Withstand tests apply specified voltage which must not cause flashover or puncture.

mcq.q: Basic Insulation Level (BIL) is expressed in terms of:
mcq.e: BIL is the peak value of the standard lightning impulse withstand voltage.

mcq.q: The induced overvoltage test on transformers is done at:
mcq.e: Higher frequency is used to avoid core saturation at overvoltage.

mcq.q: Electrostatic precipitators are used to:
o: Remove dust particles from flue gases
mcq.e: ESPs charge particles and collect them on electrodes.

mcq.q: Ozone is generated electrically using:
mcq.e: Dielectric barrier discharge converts O2 into O3.

mcq.q: In electrostatic painting, paint particles are:
o: Charged and attracted to the grounded object
mcq.e: Charged paint droplets are attracted to the earthed workpiece, improving coverage.

mcq.q: Electrostatic printing in photocopiers is based on:
mcq.e: Xerography uses a charged photoconductor to attract toner.

mcq.q: The Wright brothers made the first powered, controlled aeroplane flight in:
mcq.e: Orville and Wilbur Wright flew the Flyer at Kitty Hawk on 17 December 1903.

mcq.q: The sea-level temperature in the International Standard Atmosphere is:
mcq.e: ISA sea-level temperature is 288.15 K, i.e. 15 °C.

mcq.q: The temperature lapse rate in the ISA troposphere is:
mcq.e: ISA temperature falls linearly at 6.5 K per km up to 11 km.

mcq.q: In the ISA, between 11 km and 20 km altitude the temperature is:
mcq.e: The lower stratosphere (11-20 km) in ISA is isothermal at 216.65 K.

mcq.q: Lift on an aerofoil is defined as the aerodynamic force component:
mcq.e: Lift is perpendicular and drag is parallel to the relative wind.

mcq.q: Newton's law of viscosity gives the shear stress as τ =
mcq.e: Shear stress is proportional to the velocity gradient, with dynamic viscosity μ as the constant.

mcq.q: The Eulerian description of fluid flow:
o: Observes flow properties at fixed points in space
mcq.e: Eulerian methods describe the flow field as functions of position and time at fixed points.

mcq.q: For the NACA 2412 aerofoil, the location of maximum camber is at:
o: 40% of chord from the leading edge
mcq.e: In NACA 4-digit series, the second digit × 10 gives the position of maximum camber in % chord.
mcq.t: Lift and drag coefficients using NACA data

mcq.q: Skin friction drag arises mainly from:
o: Viscous shear stress on the surface
mcq.e: Skin friction drag is the integral of wall shear stress over the wetted surface.

mcq.q: Boundary layer separation occurs in a region of:
o: Uniform free stream with no gradient
mcq.e: Rising pressure along the flow decelerates the near-wall fluid until it reverses and separates.

mcq.q: An aircraft flying at 100 m/s has a drag of 2000 N. The power required is:
mcq.e: Power required = D × V = 2000 × 100 = 200,000 W = 200 kW.

mcq.q: For a parabolic drag polar CD = CD0 + kCL^2, minimum thrust required (maximum L/D) occurs when:
mcq.e: Minimising CD/CL gives the condition that zero-lift drag equals lift-induced drag.

mcq.q: A rigid aircraft in flight has how many degrees of freedom?
mcq.e: Three translations and three rotations give six degrees of freedom.
mcq.t: Degrees of freedom of aircraft motions

mcq.q: Hooke's law states that within the elastic limit:
o: Stress is proportional to strain squared
mcq.e: In the linear elastic range σ = E ε.

mcq.q: An aircraft that is statically stable, when disturbed, initially tends to:
o: Remain in the new disturbed position
mcq.e: Static stability means the initial restoring tendency is back toward equilibrium.

mcq.q: The section modulus of a rectangular section of width b and depth h about its neutral axis is:
mcq.e: Z = I/ymax = (bh³/12)/(h/2) = bh²/6.

mcq.q: According to Kepler's first law, a planet moves in:
o: A circle with the Sun at the centre
An ellipse with the Sun at one focus
An ellipse with the Sun at the centre
mcq.e: Kepler's first law states orbits are ellipses with the Sun at one focus.

mcq.q: Kepler's third law states that the orbital period T and semi-major axis a are related by:
mcq.e: The square of the period is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis.

mcq.q: How many classical orbital elements are needed to define a Keplerian orbit and position?
mcq.e: The six elements are a, e, i, RAAN, argument of perigee and true anomaly (or epoch).

mcq.q: A Hohmann transfer between two coplanar circular orbits uses:
mcq.e: A Hohmann transfer is an elliptical orbit tangent to both circles, entered and exited by two burns.

mcq.q: In a fly-by-wire system, pilot inputs reach the actuators as:
mcq.e: Fly-by-wire replaces mechanical linkages with electrical signalling through flight computers.

mcq.q: A push-pull rod control system transmits motion using:
o: Rigid rods in tension and compression
mcq.e: Push-pull rods carry both tensile and compressive loads.

mcq.q: In a fully powered (irreversible) flight control system, the pilot feels control loads through:
mcq.e: Irreversible actuators block aerodynamic loads, so artificial feel is provided.

mcq.q: An autopilot holding altitude primarily controls which surface in a conventional aircraft?
mcq.e: Pitch attitude, hence altitude, is controlled by the elevator.

mcq.q: Hydraulic systems in aircraft work on:
mcq.e: Pascal's law: pressure applied to a confined fluid transmits equally in all directions.

mcq.q: The component that stores hydraulic fluid under pressure to meet peak demands is the:
mcq.e: Accumulators store pressurized fluid and damp pressure surges.

mcq.q: The most common landing gear shock absorber on modern aircraft is the:
mcq.e: Oleo-pneumatic struts use oil and compressed gas to absorb landing energy.

mcq.q: A landing gear with main wheels behind the CG and a nose wheel in front is a:
mcq.e: Tricycle gear has a nose wheel ahead of the CG.

mcq.q: Piston aero-engines typically use which ignition source?
mcq.e: Dual magnetos provide independent self-powered ignition.

mcq.q: In a jet engine fuel system, fuel is atomized into the combustor by:
mcq.e: Fuel nozzles spray atomized fuel into the combustion chamber.

mcq.q: Jet engines are commonly started by:
o: Rotating the compressor with a starter (e.g., air turbine starter)
mcq.e: The starter spins the compressor to self-sustaining speed before light-off.

mcq.q: A dry sump lubrication system is characterized by:
o: Oil stored in a separate tank with scavenge pumps
mcq.e: Scavenge pumps return oil to an external tank in dry sump systems.

mcq.q: A gyroscope's property of maintaining its spin axis orientation in space is called:
mcq.e: Rigidity in space keeps the spin axis fixed unless torque acts.

mcq.q: When a torque is applied to a spinning gyroscope, the axis turns 90° in the spin direction. This is:
mcq.e: Precession is the gyroscope response to applied torque.

mcq.q: A guidance scheme where the missile follows a beam pointed at the target is:
mcq.e: Beam rider missiles stay within a radar or laser beam aimed at the target.

mcq.q: In a missile, fin actuation servos convert autopilot commands into:
mcq.e: Servos drive control fins to the commanded deflection angles.

mcq.q: The primary power source for most Earth-orbiting satellites is:
mcq.e: Solar panels with batteries supply most satellite power.

mcq.q: Spin stabilization of a spacecraft relies on:
o: Gyroscopic stiffness of a spinning body
mcq.e: Angular momentum of spin resists attitude disturbances.

mcq.q: Multi-layer insulation (MLI) on spacecraft mainly reduces heat transfer by:
mcq.e: In vacuum, heat exchange is mainly radiative, which MLI blocks.

mcq.q: Reaction wheels control spacecraft attitude by:
o: Exchanging angular momentum with the spacecraft
mcq.e: Speeding up or slowing a wheel rotates the spacecraft oppositely.

mcq.q: Green's theorem in the plane converts a line integral around a closed curve into a:
o: Double integral over the enclosed region
mcq.e: Closed integral of (P dx + Q dy) equals double integral of (dQ/dx - dP/dy) dx dy.

mcq.q: For r = x i + y j + z k, the flux of r over the sphere of radius a is:
mcq.e: div r = 3, so the flux = 3 x (4/3) pi a^3 = 4 pi a^3.

mcq.q: The Cauchy-Riemann equations in Cartesian form are:
mcq.e: For f = u + iv to be analytic, ux = vy and uy = -vx.

The bilinear transformation w = (az + b)/(cz + d) requires:
mcq.e: If ad - bc = 0 the map degenerates to a constant.

mcq.q: A bilinear transformation other than the identity has at most how many fixed points?
mcq.e: Setting z = (az + b)/(cz + d) gives a quadratic, so at most two fixed points.

mcq.q: If f(z) is analytic inside and on a simple closed curve C, the integral of f(z) dz over C is:
mcq.e: Cauchy's integral theorem gives zero for analytic functions.

mcq.q: The residue of 1/(z(z - 1)) at z = 1 is:
mcq.e: Residue = lim (z - 1) f(z) = 1/z at z = 1 = 1.

mcq.q: The singularity of sin(z)/z at z = 0 is:
mcq.e: sin z / z tends to 1 and its Laurent series has no negative powers.

mcq.q: The function e^(1/z) has at z = 0 a(n):
mcq.e: Its Laurent series has infinitely many negative powers of z.

mcq.q: The Laplace transform of e^(at) is:
mcq.e: Integral of e^(-st) e^(at) from 0 to infinity = 1/(s - a) for s > a.

mcq.q: The Laplace transform of t^2 is:
The final value theorem states that lim (t to infinity) f(t) equals:
mcq.e: Provided the limit exists, f(infinity) = lim s->0 of sF(s).

mcq.q: The Laplace transform of t sin t is:
The complementary function of y'' - 3y' + 2y = 0 is:
o: c1 cos x + c2 sin x
mcq.e: Auxiliary equation m^2 - 3m + 2 = 0 gives m = 1, 2.

mcq.q: Euler's homogeneous equation is reduced to constant coefficients by substituting:
mcq.e: With x = e^z, x d/dx becomes d/dz.

mcq.q: The particular integral of (D^2 - 4) y = e^(3x) is:
mcq.e: Replacing D by 3 gives e^(3x)/(9 - 4) = e^(3x)/5.

mcq.q: Legendre's linear equation is reduced to constant coefficients by substituting:
mcq.e: For (ax + b)^n terms, ax + b = e^z converts (ax+b) d/dx into a d/dz.

mcq.q: Vorticity in a flow field is defined as:
mcq.e: Vorticity ω = ∇ x V, twice the local angular velocity.

mcq.q: Stokes' theorem relates the circulation around a closed curve to the:
o: Flux of vorticity through a surface bounded by the curve
mcq.e: Γ = ∮V·ds = ∬(∇ x V)·dS.

mcq.q: Kelvin's circulation theorem states that, in inviscid barotropic flow with conservative body forces, circulation around a closed fluid curve:
mcq.e: DΓ/Dt = 0 under these conditions.

mcq.q: A flow is called barotropic when:
o: Density is a function of pressure only
mcq.e: In barotropic flow ρ = ρ(p), which makes the baroclinic term vanish.

mcq.q: The stream function of a uniform flow of speed U along the x-axis is:
mcq.e: u = ∂ψ/∂y = U gives ψ = Uy.

mcq.q: In a free (irrotational) vortex, the tangential velocity varies with radius r as:
mcq.e: Vθ = Γ/(2πr) for a free vortex.

mcq.q: Superposition of a uniform flow and a 2-D source produces flow over a:
mcq.e: A source in a uniform stream gives a semi-infinite Rankine half body.

mcq.q: For ideal flow past a circular cylinder without circulation, the pressure coefficient at θ = 90° is:
mcq.e: Cp = 1 - 4 sin^2θ gives -3 at the top of the cylinder.

mcq.q: The Kutta-Joukowski theorem gives lift per unit span as:
mcq.e: L' = ρ∞ V∞ Γ for any 2-D body with circulation Γ.

mcq.q: The Blasius theorem is used to calculate:
o: Forces and moments on a body in 2-D potential flow
mcq.e: It expresses force and moment as contour integrals of the complex velocity.

mcq.q: The Kutta condition requires that the flow at a sharp trailing edge:
mcq.e: It fixes the circulation so flow leaves the trailing edge smoothly.

mcq.q: Under the Joukowski transformation z = ζ + c^2/ζ, a circle of radius c centred at the origin maps to a:
mcq.e: The circle maps to a slit from -2c to 2c, i.e. a plate of length 4c.

mcq.q: According to thin airfoil theory, the lift curve slope is:
mcq.e: Thin airfoil theory gives dCl/dα = 2π per radian.

mcq.q: The Biot-Savart law is used to find the:
o: Velocity induced by a vortex filament
mcq.e: It gives the induced velocity from a vortex segment of given strength.

mcq.q: Thin airfoil theory places the aerodynamic centre at:
mcq.e: The moment about the quarter-chord point is independent of α.

mcq.q: An elliptic wing of aspect ratio 8 has CL = 0.8. Its induced drag coefficient is about:
Mach number is defined as the ratio of:
o: Speed of sound to flow velocity
Flow velocity to local speed of sound
mcq.e: M = V/a.

mcq.q: The Mach number just downstream of a normal shock is always:
mcq.e: A normal shock always turns supersonic flow into subsonic flow.

mcq.q: Across a normal shock, the stagnation pressure:
mcq.e: Entropy rises across the shock, so total pressure drops.

mcq.q: Clapeyron's three-moment equation is used to analyse:
mcq.e: It relates support moments at three consecutive supports of a continuous beam.

mcq.q: In the transformed section method, the width of the stiffer material is multiplied by:
mcq.e: Widths are scaled by n = E2/E1 to form an equivalent single-material section.

mcq.q: For a statically determinate plane truss with j joints, the number of members m is:
mcq.e: A just-rigid plane truss satisfies m = 2j - 3.

mcq.q: A statically determinate space truss with j joints has how many members?
mcq.e: For space trusses, m = 3j - 6.

mcq.q: Strain energy stored in a bar of length L, area A under axial load P is:
mcq.e: U = P^2 L/(2AE) for a linearly elastic bar.

mcq.q: Castigliano's second theorem gives deflection under load P as:
mcq.e: Deflection in the direction of P equals the partial derivative of strain energy with respect to P.

mcq.q: Strain energy per unit volume at stress 200 MPa with E = 200 GPa is:
For a linearly elastic structure, complementary energy is:
mcq.e: With a linear load-deflection curve the areas above and below are equal.

mcq.q: Euler's critical load for a pinned-pinned column of length L is:
mcq.e: For pinned ends, effective length = L, so Pcr = π^2 EI/L^2.

mcq.q: Effective length of a column fixed at one end and free at the other is:
mcq.e: A cantilever column buckles as half of a pinned column of length 2L.

mcq.q: Euler load of a fixed-fixed column is how many times that of an identical pinned-pinned column?
mcq.e: Effective length L/2 makes Pcr four times larger.

mcq.q: Inelastic buckling of columns is commonly predicted using the:
mcq.e: Engesser's tangent modulus theory replaces E with Et beyond the proportional limit.

mcq.q: The distortion energy theory of failure is also known as the:
mcq.e: Distortion energy theory is the von Mises (Hencky) criterion.

mcq.q: By von Mises theory, shear yield strength in terms of tensile yield σy is:
mcq.e: τy = σy/sqrt(3) ≈ 0.577σy.

mcq.q: For fully reversed cyclic loading, the stress ratio R = σmin/σmax is:
mcq.e: Equal and opposite peaks give R = -1.

mcq.q: The endurance limit on an S-N curve is the stress below which:
o: The material can endure infinite cycles
mcq.e: Below the endurance limit, steels can sustain indefinitely many cycles.

mcq.q: Efficiency of a riveted joint is defined as:
o: Least strength of joint / strength of solid plate
mcq.e: Joint efficiency compares the weakest failure mode with the unpunched plate.

mcq.q: Throat thickness of a fillet weld with leg size s is:
mcq.e: For an equal-leg 45 degree fillet, throat = s cos 45 = 0.707 s.

mcq.q: Which is a failure mode of a riveted joint?
mcq.e: Riveted joints fail by rivet shear, plate crushing or plate tearing.

mcq.q: A normal shock in an intake makes the downstream flow:
mcq.e: Flow behind a normal shock is always subsonic.

mcq.q: Pressure recovery of an intake is defined as:
mcq.e: Pressure recovery is the ratio of exit to freestream stagnation pressure.

mcq.q: A subsonic intake acts primarily as a:
mcq.e: Subsonic intakes decelerate flow, raising static pressure like a diffuser.

mcq.q: The starting problem of a supersonic intake is overcome by:
mcq.e: Overspeeding or enlarging throat lets the shock be swallowed.

mcq.q: In a centrifugal compressor, flow leaves the impeller in the:
mcq.e: Air enters axially and leaves the impeller radially.

mcq.q: Euler's work per unit mass in a turbomachine is:
mcq.e: Euler's equation: W = U2 Cw2 - U1 Cw1.

mcq.q: Degree of reaction 0.5 in an axial compressor means:
o: Equal static enthalpy rise in rotor and stator
mcq.e: 50% reaction splits static enthalpy rise equally between rotor and stator.

mcq.q: Surge in a compressor occurs at:
o: Low mass flow and high pressure ratio
High mass flow and low pressure ratio
mcq.e: At low flow and high pressure ratio, flow breaks down and reverses (surge).

mcq.q: In an impulse turbine stage, pressure drop occurs:
mcq.e: In a pure impulse stage the entire pressure drop is in the nozzles.

mcq.q: Film cooling of turbine blades works by:
o: Ejecting coolant air to form a protective layer on the surface
mcq.e: Coolant ejected through holes forms an insulating film over the blade.

mcq.q: Free vortex design satisfies:
mcq.e: In free vortex flow, tangential velocity times radius is constant.

mcq.q: Radial inflow turbines are typically used in:
mcq.e: Radial turbines suit small mass flows such as turbochargers.

mcq.q: An afterburner is used to:
o: Increase thrust by burning fuel after the turbine
mcq.e: Reheating exhaust gas raises jet velocity and thrust.

mcq.q: The combustor type with a single annular liner around the engine is the:
mcq.e: Annular combustors use a single continuous annular liner.

mcq.q: To accelerate flow to supersonic speeds, a nozzle must be:
mcq.e: Supersonic exit flow needs a throat followed by a divergent section.

mcq.q: In a convergent nozzle, the maximum exit Mach number is:
mcq.e: A convergent nozzle chokes at Mach 1 at its exit.

mcq.q: A ramjet has:
mcq.e: Ramjets compress air by ram effect without rotating machinery.

mcq.q: The ideal thermodynamic cycle of a ramjet is the:
mcq.e: Ramjets follow the Brayton (constant pressure heat addition) cycle.

mcq.q: A ramjet cannot produce static thrust because:
o: There is no ram compression at zero speed
mcq.e: Without forward speed there is no ram compression.

mcq.q: In an integral rocket ramjet, the solid rocket booster is housed:
mcq.e: The booster propellant occupies the ramjet combustor and is ejected after burnout.

mcq.q: A four-bar chain has how many binary links?
mcq.e: A four-bar mechanism consists of four binary links with four turning pairs.

mcq.q: Grubler's criterion for planar mechanisms with only lower pairs gives degrees of freedom F =
mcq.e: F = 3(n - 1) - 2j, where n = links and j = lower pairs.

mcq.q: The follower motion with uniform acceleration and retardation gives a displacement diagram that is:
mcq.e: Constant acceleration gives a parabolic displacement curve.

mcq.q: The Whitworth quick return mechanism is an inversion of the:
mcq.e: Whitworth quick return is obtained by fixing the crank of a slider crank chain.

mcq.q: The law of gearing requires the common normal at the point of contact to pass through the:
mcq.e: This ensures a constant angular velocity ratio.

mcq.q: Module of a gear is defined as:
mcq.e: m = D/T in mm.

mcq.q: The standard pressure angles commonly used for involute gears are:
mcq.e: 14.5 and 20 degree pressure angles are standard.

mcq.q: In a simple gear train, driver has 20 teeth at 300 rpm and driven has 60 teeth. Driven speed is:
The ratio of tensions in a flat belt drive is given by T1/T2 =
mcq.e: From belt friction equilibrium, T1/T2 = e^(mu theta).

mcq.q: A screw is self-locking when the friction angle phi and helix angle alpha satisfy:
mcq.e: If friction angle exceeds helix angle, the load cannot lower by itself.

mcq.q: Torque transmitted by a single-plate clutch under uniform wear theory is proportional to:
mcq.e: T = mu W R with R = (r1 + r2)/2 under uniform wear.

mcq.q: Compared to sliding friction, rolling friction is generally:
mcq.e: Rolling resistance is much less than sliding friction.

mcq.q: D'Alembert's principle converts a dynamic problem into an equivalent:
mcq.e: Adding inertia forces allows static equilibrium equations to be used.

mcq.q: A two-force member in equilibrium has forces that are:
mcq.e: Two forces balance only if equal, opposite and along the same line.

mcq.q: The inertia force on a body of mass m with acceleration a acts:
mcq.e: Inertia force = -ma, opposite to the acceleration.

mcq.q: A three-force member in equilibrium must have the three forces:
o: Summing to zero moment only about one point
mcq.e: Three non-parallel coplanar forces in equilibrium must be concurrent.

mcq.q: Natural frequency of a spring-mass system is omega_n =
mcq.e: omega_n = sqrt(k/m) rad/s.

mcq.q: A system is critically damped when the damping ratio is:
mcq.e: Critical damping corresponds to zeta = 1.

mcq.q: Vibration isolation (transmissibility < 1) occurs when frequency ratio exceeds:
mcq.e: TR < 1 for omega/omega_n > sqrt(2).

mcq.q: Complete dynamic balancing of rotating masses in different planes requires:
o: Both resultant force and resultant couple zero
mcq.e: Dynamic balance needs both force and couple balance.

mcq.q: In steady level unaccelerated flight, lift equals:
mcq.e: In level flight L = W and T = D.

mcq.q: The parabolic drag polar is written as:
mcq.e: CD = CD0 + K CL^2, with K = 1/(πeAR).

mcq.q: For minimum drag in level flight with a parabolic polar:
mcq.e: Minimum drag occurs when CD0 = K CL^2.

mcq.q: Drag due to lift is called:
mcq.e: Induced drag arises from wing-tip vortices due to lift generation.

mcq.q: Load factor n in a level coordinated turn with bank angle φ is:
mcq.e: n = L/W = 1/cos φ.

mcq.q: In a 60° banked level turn, the load factor is:
The V-n diagram represents:
o: Flight envelope of speed vs load factor
mcq.e: The V-n diagram defines structural and aerodynamic limits of load factor with speed.

mcq.q: For a jet aircraft, maximum endurance occurs at the flight condition of:
mcq.e: Jet endurance is maximised at maximum L/D (minimum drag).

mcq.q: A rigid aircraft in space has how many degrees of freedom?
mcq.e: Three translations and three rotations give six degrees of freedom.

mcq.q: For static longitudinal stability, the slope dCm/dα must be:
mcq.e: A negative Cm-α slope produces restoring pitching moments.

mcq.q: The CG position at which dCm/dα = 0 (stick fixed) is the:
mcq.e: The stick-fixed neutral point is where the aircraft becomes neutrally stable.

mcq.q: Static margin is the distance between:
o: Neutral point and CG (as fraction of chord)
mcq.e: Static margin = (xNP - xCG)/c.

mcq.q: The rolling moment produced by sideslip due to wing dihedral is called:
mcq.e: Dihedral effect creates a restoring rolling moment in sideslip.

mcq.q: Yawing of an aircraft opposite to the direction of roll when ailerons are deflected is:
mcq.e: Higher drag on the down-going aileron's wing causes adverse yaw.

mcq.q: The tendency of an aircraft to align itself with the relative wind is:
mcq.e: Weathercocking is static directional stability provided mainly by the vertical tail.

mcq.q: Aileron reversal at high speed is caused by:
mcq.e: Aeroelastic wing twist can cancel and reverse aileron effectiveness.

mcq.q: The short-period mode is a mode of:
mcq.e: Short period and phugoid are the longitudinal modes.

mcq.q: The phugoid mode involves slow exchange of:
o: Kinetic and potential energy at nearly constant α
mcq.e: Phugoid is a long-period oscillation in speed and altitude.

mcq.q: Dutch roll is a coupled oscillation of:
mcq.e: Dutch roll is a lateral-directional oscillation combining rolling and yawing.

mcq.q: A sustained autorotation in a steep helical descent at stalled angle of attack is a:
mcq.e: A spin is an aggravated stall with autorotation.

mcq.q: The Van Allen radiation belts consist of:
o: Charged particles trapped by Earth's magnetic field
mcq.e: The Van Allen belts are zones of energetic protons and electrons trapped in the geomagnetic field.

mcq.q: Erosion of spacecraft surface materials by atomic oxygen is a major concern in:
mcq.e: Atomic oxygen is abundant in the residual atmosphere at LEO altitudes and erodes polymers.
mcq.t: Effect of space environment on materials

mcq.q: The lifetime of a satellite in low Earth orbit is mainly limited by:
mcq.e: Drag in the upper atmosphere causes orbital decay and eventual re-entry.

mcq.q: A single event upset (SEU) in spacecraft electronics is caused by:
o: A high-energy charged particle striking a device
mcq.e: An energetic ion deposits charge in a sensitive node and flips a stored bit.
mcq.t: Effect of space environment on materials

mcq.q: Kepler's second law states that the line joining a planet to the Sun sweeps:
mcq.e: The areal velocity of a planet is constant, so equal areas are swept in equal times.

mcq.q: Kepler's second law is a consequence of the conservation of:
mcq.e: Under a central force angular momentum is conserved, which makes areal velocity constant.

mcq.q: How many Lagrange (libration) points exist in the circular restricted three-body problem?
mcq.e: There are three collinear points (L1, L2, L3) and two triangular points (L4, L5).

mcq.q: The triangular Lagrange points L4 and L5 are stable when the mass ratio μ is less than about:
mcq.e: Routh's criterion gives linear stability of L4/L5 for μ < 0.0385.

mcq.q: The minimum-energy two-impulse transfer between coplanar circular orbits is the:
mcq.e: The Hohmann transfer ellipse is tangent to both orbits and minimises Δv for two impulses.

mcq.q: Cowell's method of orbit perturbation analysis involves:
o: Integrating only the deviation from a reference orbit
Direct numerical integration of the total acceleration
mcq.e: Cowell's method integrates the full equations of motion including all perturbing accelerations; Encke's integrates the deviation.

mcq.q: The dominant perturbation due to Earth's oblateness is represented by the coefficient:
mcq.e: J2, the second zonal harmonic, models the equatorial bulge and is the largest gravitational perturbation.

mcq.q: For a prograde (i < 90°) orbit, the J2 perturbation causes the line of nodes to:
mcq.e: The nodal rate is proportional to -cos i, so for i < 90° the RAAN regresses.
mcq.t: Method of variations of orbital elements

mcq.q: The radius of the sphere of influence of a planet of mass m orbiting the Sun (mass M) at distance a is:
mcq.e: Laplace's sphere of influence radius is r = a (m/M)^(2/5).

mcq.q: Lambert's problem is to determine:
o: The escape velocity from a planet
The orbit connecting two position vectors in a given time of flight
The period from the semi-major axis
The radius of the sphere of influence
mcq.e: Lambert's problem finds the conic joining two positions for a specified transfer time.

mcq.q: The patched-conic approximation models an interplanetary trajectory as:
o: A single ellipse about the target planet
Two-body conic segments joined at sphere-of-influence boundaries
An n-body numerically integrated path only
mcq.e: In the patched-conic method each phase is a two-body conic, patched at SOI boundaries.

mcq.q: The hyperbolic excess speed v∞ of a spacecraft is its speed:
o: Remaining at infinite distance from the planet
mcq.e: From the energy equation v² = v∞² + 2μ/r, v∞ is the residual speed as r tends to infinity.
mcq.t: Trajectory estimation about the target planet

mcq.q: During the ballistic (free-flight) phase above the atmosphere, a missile moves mainly under:
mcq.e: After burnout and outside the atmosphere only gravity acts on the missile.

mcq.q: For a spherical, non-rotating Earth, the free-flight path of a ballistic missile is part of:
o: An ellipse with Earth's centre at one focus
A circle centred on the launch point
mcq.e: Sub-orbital free flight under inverse-square gravity follows a conic, an ellipse with one focus at Earth's centre.

mcq.q: Neglecting air resistance and Earth's curvature, maximum range is obtained at a launch elevation of:
mcq.e: Range = v² sin 2θ / g, which is maximum when 2θ = 90°.

mcq.q: Influence coefficients in ballistic missile analysis express:
o: Drag coefficient of the re-entry vehicle
Change in range per unit error in burnout parameters
mcq.e: They are partial derivatives of range with respect to burnout velocity, flight path angle and position errors.

mcq.q: In the force-voltage analogy, a mechanical spring (stiffness K) corresponds to:
mcq.e: Spring force Kx corresponds to q/C, so K maps to 1/C.

mcq.q: In the force-voltage analogy, viscous friction coefficient B corresponds to:
mcq.e: Damping force B v corresponds to voltage R i.

mcq.q: Thermal resistance in a thermal system is analogous to electrical:
mcq.e: Temperature difference drives heat flow through thermal resistance like voltage through resistance.

mcq.q: Two springs of stiffness k each connected in series give equivalent stiffness:
mcq.e: For springs in series 1/keq = 1/k + 1/k, so keq = k/2.

mcq.q: A closed loop system differs from an open loop system by having:
mcq.e: Closed loop systems compare output with input via feedback.

mcq.q: Closed loop transfer function with forward G and negative feedback H is:
mcq.e: For negative feedback, C/R = G/(1 + GH).

mcq.q: Two blocks G1 and G2 in cascade reduce to:
mcq.e: Cascaded transfer functions multiply.

mcq.q: Mason's gain formula gives the overall transmittance using:
o: Forward paths, loops and graph determinant
mcq.e: T = Σ Pk Δk / Δ with Δ formed from loop gains.

mcq.q: A linear system is stable if all closed loop poles lie in the:
mcq.e: Poles with negative real parts give decaying responses.

mcq.q: In the Routh array, the number of sign changes in the first column equals the number of:
mcq.e: Each sign change indicates a root in the right half plane.

mcq.q: Root locus branches start at open loop:
mcq.e: At K = 0, closed loop poles coincide with open loop poles.

mcq.q: In a Bode magnitude plot, a simple pole contributes a slope of:
mcq.e: Each simple pole adds -20 dB/decade beyond its corner frequency.

mcq.q: The Z-transform of the unit step sequence is:
mcq.e: Σ z^-n for n≥0 gives z/(z-1).

mcq.q: A discrete system is stable if all its poles lie:
o: Inside the unit circle in the z-plane
mcq.e: Stability in z-domain requires |z| < 1 for all poles.

mcq.q: The integral term in a PID controller primarily:
mcq.e: Integral action accumulates error, driving steady-state error to zero.

mcq.q: The mapping between s-plane and z-plane for sampling period T is:
mcq.e: Sampling maps s to z through z = e^(sT).

mcq.q: The natural frequency of an undamped spring-mass system is:
mcq.e: From m x'' + k x = 0, wn = sqrt(k/m) rad/s.

mcq.q: A critically damped system has a damping ratio of:
mcq.e: Critical damping occurs when c = 2 sqrt(km), i.e. zeta = 1.

mcq.q: The logarithmic decrement of an underdamped system is defined as:
mcq.e: It is the natural log of the ratio of two successive amplitudes.

mcq.q: Transmissibility becomes less than 1 (vibration isolation) only when the frequency ratio exceeds:
mcq.e: For all damping values, TR = 1 at r = sqrt(2) and TR < 1 beyond it.

mcq.q: An undamped two degree of freedom system has how many natural frequencies?
mcq.e: Number of natural frequencies equals the number of degrees of freedom.

mcq.q: An undamped dynamic vibration absorber reduces the main mass amplitude to zero when its natural frequency equals:
mcq.e: Tuning sqrt(k2/m2) to the forcing frequency makes the absorber cancel the force on the main mass.

mcq.q: Principal coordinates are those in which the equations of motion are:
mcq.e: In principal coordinates each equation involves only one coordinate.

mcq.q: For distinct modes i and j, the orthogonality condition with respect to the mass matrix is:
mcq.e: Normal modes of different frequency are M-orthogonal (and K-orthogonal).

mcq.q: The speed of transverse waves on a taut string with tension T and mass per unit length rho is:
mcq.e: The wave equation for a string gives c^2 = T/rho.

mcq.q: A continuous elastic system has how many natural frequencies?
o: Equal to its length in metres
mcq.e: Distributed mass and stiffness give infinite degrees of freedom.

mcq.q: The fundamental frequency of a string of length L fixed at both ends is:
mcq.e: The fundamental has wavelength 2L, so f1 = c/(2L).

mcq.q: The speed of torsional waves in a uniform circular shaft is:
mcq.e: Torsional wave equation gives c^2 = G/rho, with G the shear modulus.

mcq.q: Rayleigh's method is based on the principle that:
o: Maximum kinetic energy equals maximum potential energy
mcq.e: For a conservative system, equating maximum KE and PE yields the frequency.

mcq.q: Dunkerley's method gives a fundamental frequency that is:
o: A lower bound to the exact value
An upper bound to the exact value
mcq.e: Neglecting higher-mode terms makes Dunkerley's estimate lower than the exact value.

mcq.q: Holzer's method is mainly used for:
mcq.e: It is a tabular trial-frequency method for torsional systems.

mcq.q: Matrix iteration using the dynamical (flexibility-based) matrix converges first to the:
mcq.e: Repeated multiplication by the flexibility-based matrix amplifies the mode with largest 1/w^2.

mcq.q: Collar's aeroelastic triangle involves which three types of forces?
mcq.e: Aeroelasticity is the interaction of aerodynamic, elastic and inertial forces.

mcq.q: Flutter is classified as a:
mcq.e: Flutter involves aerodynamic, elastic and inertial forces in self-excited oscillation.

mcq.q: Wing divergence is a static aeroelastic instability involving:
mcq.e: Aerodynamic twisting moment overcomes torsional stiffness; inertia plays no role.

mcq.q: Above the aileron reversal speed, deflecting the aileron produces:
o: A rolling moment opposite to that intended
mcq.e: Aileron-induced wing twist reduces lift so much that the net rolling moment reverses.

mcq.q: The ideal rocket (Tsiolkovsky) equation gives Δv as:
mcq.e: Δv = ve ln(m0/mf), where ve is effective exhaust velocity.

mcq.q: For static stability of a finned rocket, the centre of pressure must lie:

mcq.e: With CP aft of CG, a disturbance produces a restoring moment.

mcq.q: A rocket with exhaust velocity 3000 m/s has mass ratio m0/mf = e. Its ideal Δv is:
Nozzle thrust is maximum for a given chamber condition when exit pressure equals:
mcq.e: Optimum expansion occurs at pe = pa.

mcq.q: The burn rate of a solid propellant is commonly expressed as:
mcq.e: Saint Robert's (Vieille's) law gives r = aP^n.

mcq.q: The most common oxidiser in composite solid propellants is:
mcq.e: Ammonium perchlorate is the standard oxidiser in composite propellants.

mcq.q: For stable operation of a solid motor, the burn-rate pressure exponent n must be:
mcq.e: With n < 1 chamber pressure returns to equilibrium after a disturbance.

mcq.q: In solid motor design, the ratio Kn is defined as:
o: Burning surface area to throat area
mcq.e: Kn = Ab/At strongly controls chamber pressure.

mcq.q: A typical cryogenic bipropellant combination is:
mcq.e: LOX/LH2 must be stored at very low temperatures.

mcq.q: Hypergolic propellants are those that:
mcq.e: Hypergolic fuel and oxidiser ignite upon mixing.

mcq.q: Pogo instability in liquid rockets is:
o: Longitudinal oscillation from coupling of structure and propulsion
mcq.e: Vehicle vibration modulates propellant feed and thrust, reinforcing the oscillation.

mcq.q: The vacuum specific impulse of LOX/LH2 engines is typically about:
mcq.e: LOX/LH2 engines deliver roughly 440-460 s in vacuum.

mcq.q: The main advantage of multi-staging is that it:
o: Discards dead mass to achieve higher Δv
mcq.e: Dropping empty stages improves effective mass ratio.

mcq.q: An inertial navigation system in a launch vehicle uses:
mcq.e: It integrates accelerometer and gyro outputs to determine position and attitude.

mcq.q: Two stages each provide an ideal Δv of 3 km/s. The ideal total Δv is:
mcq.e: Ideal stage Δv values add, giving 6 km/s.

mcq.q: Gimballing the main engine of a launch vehicle mainly provides control in:
mcq.e: Tilting the thrust vector produces pitch and yaw moments.

mcq.q: Inconel, used in hot rocket engine parts, is a:
mcq.e: Inconel is a nickel-chromium superalloy for high temperatures.

mcq.q: A static fire test of a rocket motor is a:
o: Ground firing with the motor held fixed
mcq.e: The motor is fired on a test stand to measure thrust and performance.

mcq.q: Carbon-carbon composites are widely used in rockets for:
mcq.e: They retain strength at very high temperatures and resist ablation.

mcq.q: In low Earth orbit, a major material degradation agent for polymer surfaces is:
mcq.e: Atomic oxygen erodes polymers and composites in LEO.

mcq.q: A ferroelectric material is characterised by:

mcq.q: The magnetic susceptibility of a diamagnetic material is:

mcq.q: Above its Curie temperature, a ferromagnet becomes:
mcq.e: Thermal energy destroys spontaneous alignment above Tc.

mcq.e: Phase matching keeps fundamental and harmonic waves in step so power builds up.

mcq.e: Both ends fixed gives Le = L/2.

mcq.q: The Southwell plot is used to determine experimentally the:
mcq.e: Plotting δ/P vs δ gives a line whose inverse slope is P_cr.

mcq.q: A cantilever column (fixed-free) has buckling load compared with a pinned-pinned column of same L:
mcq.e: Le = 2L, so P_cr = π^2EI/(4L^2), one quarter.

mcq.q: The maximum principal stress theory (Rankine) is best suited for:
mcq.e: Brittle materials fail by fracture when maximum principal stress reaches the limit.

mcq.q: The maximum shear stress theory is associated with:
mcq.e: Tresca/Guest theory predicts yield when max shear reaches half the yield stress.

mcq.q: The distortion energy theory is also called:
mcq.e: von Mises (Huber-Hencky) theory is based on distortion energy.

mcq.q: The octahedral shear stress theory gives the same results as:
mcq.e: Octahedral shear stress criterion is equivalent to von Mises.

mcq.q: Thermal stress in a fully restrained bar heated by ΔT is:
mcq.e: Prevented strain α ΔT gives stress σ = E α ΔT.

mcq.q: A load suddenly applied (dropped from zero height) produces stress equal to:
mcq.e: For sudden loading σ = 2P/A.

mcq.q: Failure under repeated cyclic stresses below the ultimate strength is called:
mcq.e: Fatigue is progressive failure under cyclic loading.

mcq.q: Stress relaxation is the decrease of stress with time under:
mcq.e: At constant strain, stress decreases with time due to viscoelastic/creep effects.

o: Coincides with the axis of symmetry
Is perpendicular to the beam axis

mcq.e: If the load plane is not a principal plane, bending occurs about both axes simultaneously.

Not perpendicular to the plane of loading

The shear centre of a section is the point through which a shear load produces:

mcq.q: In a thin-walled open section, the shear flow at a free edge is:
mcq.e: No shear can be transmitted across a free (unloaded) edge, so q = 0 there.

Outside the section, on the side of the web away from the flanges
mcq.e: Flange shear flows create a moment balanced only if the load acts outside the web.

mcq.q: The torsion constant J of a thin-walled open section made of thin rectangles is approximately:
mcq.e: Each thin rectangle contributes b t^3/3 for St Venant torsion.

All cells have the same rate of twist

mcq.q: In Wagner's tension field theory for thin webs, the diagonal tension angle is often assumed close to:
mcq.e: After web buckling, load is carried by diagonal tension, commonly taken at about 45 degrees.

mcq.q: The critical buckling stress of a thin plate varies with thickness t and width b as:
mcq.e: sigma_cr = k pi^2 E/(12(1 - nu^2)) (t/b)^2.

mcq.e: For a/b equal to an integer the minimum k = 4 for simply supported edges.

o: Overall Euler buckling of a long column
Local buckling followed by local failure of its elements
mcq.e: Crippling is local instability and failure of the plate elements of short sections.

mcq.e: FAR 23 specifies 3.8 (normal), 4.4 (utility) and 6.0 (aerobatic).

mcq.q: In a canard configuration, the horizontal surface is located:
mcq.e: A canard is a foreplane placed forward of the wing.

mcq.q: High-wing layouts are common on cargo aircraft mainly because they:
o: Allow a low fuselage floor for loading
Eliminate the need for a tail
mcq.e: A high wing lets the fuselage sit close to the ground for easy loading.

mcq.q: In a T-tail configuration, the horizontal stabilizer is mounted:
o: On top of the vertical fin
mcq.e: A T-tail places the tailplane atop the fin.

mcq.q: A 3-view drawing of an airplane shows:

The cruise-segment weight fraction for a jet is derived from which equation?
mcq.e: The Breguet range equation relates range to ln(Wi-1/Wi).

mcq.q: Wing loading of an aircraft is defined as:
mcq.e: Wing loading W/S is weight per unit wing area.

mcq.q: Which power plant is generally most efficient for low-speed short-haul aircraft (about M 0.4-0.6)?
mcq.e: Turboprops give high propulsive efficiency at moderate subsonic speeds.

mcq.q: Modern subsonic airliners mostly use which engine type?
mcq.e: High-bypass turbofans give low fuel consumption at high subsonic speeds.

mcq.q: A structural advantage of wing-mounted engines is:
o: No asymmetric thrust on engine failure
mcq.e: Engine weight on the wing counteracts lift-induced bending moments.

mcq.q: Rear-fuselage-mounted engines reduce engine-out yawing moment because:
o: Engines are close to the aircraft centreline
mcq.e: A small lateral arm gives a small asymmetric thrust moment.

mcq.q: A wing with span 30 m and area 90 m^2 has aspect ratio:
Increasing wing aspect ratio primarily reduces:
mcq.e: Induced drag coefficient is inversely proportional to aspect ratio.

mcq.q: Wing sweep is used on high-speed aircraft mainly to:
mcq.e: Sweep reduces the effective normal Mach number over the wing.

mcq.q: A V-n diagram plots:
mcq.e: The V-n diagram defines the flight envelope in load factor and speed.

mcq.q: A tricycle landing gear consists of:
o: A nose wheel and two main gears
A tail wheel and two main gears
mcq.e: Tricycle gear has a nose gear ahead of the CG and mains behind it.

mcq.q: Which device commonly absorbs landing impact energy in aircraft gear?
mcq.e: Oleo struts use oil and compressed gas to absorb and dissipate energy.

mcq.q: Which control surface primarily controls pitch?
mcq.e: Elevators on the horizontal tail control pitch.

mcq.q: A horn balance on a control surface is used to:
o: Reduce hinge moment and stick force
mcq.e: Area ahead of the hinge line partly balances aerodynamic hinge moments.

mcq.q: A closed circuit wind tunnel is also called a:
mcq.e: The return-circuit (closed) tunnel is the Gottingen type; the open circuit is Eiffel type.

mcq.q: Reynolds number is the ratio of:
mcq.e: Re = ρVL/μ, the ratio of inertia to viscous forces.

mcq.q: The contraction cone in a low speed tunnel mainly serves to:
o: Accelerate the flow and reduce turbulence in the test section
mcq.e: Contraction increases velocity and reduces relative turbulence.

mcq.q: Energy ratio of a wind tunnel is the ratio of:
o: Power input to test section kinetic energy
Test section kinetic energy flux to power input
mcq.e: ER = kinetic energy flux in test section / input power; it can exceed 1.

mcq.q: A blowdown supersonic tunnel uses:
o: High-pressure air stored in tanks discharged through the test section
mcq.e: Stored high-pressure air is released through a nozzle and test section.

mcq.q: To obtain supersonic flow in the test section, the nozzle must be:
mcq.e: A C-D nozzle is required to accelerate flow beyond Mach 1.

mcq.q: The Mach number in a supersonic test section is set mainly by:
o: Area ratio of the nozzle exit to throat
mcq.e: For isentropic flow, test section Mach number depends on A/A*.

mcq.q: Transonic tunnels use slotted or perforated walls to:
mcq.e: Ventilated walls alleviate choking and shock reflections near Mach 1.

mcq.q: A shock tube consists of a driver and driven section separated by a:
mcq.e: Rupture of the diaphragm generates the shock wave.

mcq.q: Air in hypersonic tunnels is heated before expansion to:
o: Prevent liquefaction of air in the test section
mcq.e: Expansion to very high Mach numbers drops temperature enough to liquefy air without heating.

mcq.q: A gun tunnel compresses test gas using a:
o: Chemical explosion in the test section
Light piston driven down a barrel
mcq.e: A free piston compresses and heats the test gas in a gun tunnel.

mcq.q: Captive trajectory system tests are used for:
mcq.e: CTS moves a store model to simulate its separation trajectory from the aircraft.

mcq.q: A six component balance measures:
mcq.e: Six components are lift, drag, side force and roll, pitch, yaw moments.

mcq.q: A pitot-static tube measures:
o: Total and static pressure to give velocity
mcq.e: Velocity follows from the difference between total and static pressure.

mcq.q: Hot-wire anemometry is best suited to measure:
mcq.e: Hot wires have high frequency response for velocity fluctuations.

mcq.q: A three component balance usually measures:

mcq.q: Tufts attached to a model surface are used to show:
mcq.e: Tufts align with local flow and flutter in separated regions.

mcq.q: The schlieren method is sensitive to the:
mcq.e: Schlieren responds to the first derivative (gradient) of density.

mcq.q: The shadowgraph method responds to the:

mcq.q: Particle Image Velocimetry measures velocity from:
o: Displacement of seed particles between two laser-illuminated images
mcq.e: PIV cross-correlates particle images over a known time interval.

mcq.q: A fibre of effectively continuous length is called a:
mcq.e: Filaments are continuous; staple fibres have limited length.

mcq.q: Cotton is chemically composed mainly of:
mcq.e: Cotton is about 90% cellulose.

mcq.q: The protein present in wool fibre is:
mcq.e: Wool is a keratin fibre.

mcq.q: The gum that binds the two fibroin filaments in raw silk is:
mcq.e: Sericin coats fibroin and is removed by degumming.

mcq.q: Viscose rayon is regenerated from:
mcq.e: Viscose is made by dissolving cellulose from wood pulp.

mcq.q: In the viscose process, alkali cellulose is reacted with:
mcq.e: Xanthation with CS2 forms cellulose xanthate.

mcq.q: Lyocell (Tencel) is produced by dissolving cellulose in:
mcq.e: Lyocell uses direct solvent NMMO in a closed-loop process.

mcq.q: Acetate rayon is made by reacting cellulose with:
mcq.e: Acetylation of cellulose forms cellulose acetate.

mcq.q: PET polyester is made from terephthalic acid and:
mcq.e: PET is polyethylene terephthalate.

mcq.q: Nylon 6 is produced from:
mcq.e: Ring-opening polymerization of caprolactam gives nylon 6.

mcq.q: Polyester and nylon fibres are commonly produced by:
mcq.e: Both are thermoplastic and melt spun.

mcq.q: The most common precursor for carbon fibre is:
mcq.e: PAN is the dominant carbon fibre precursor.

mcq.q: Kevlar is an example of a/an:
mcq.e: Kevlar is poly-para-phenylene terephthalamide.

mcq.q: Nomex is known mainly for its:
mcq.e: Nomex is a meta-aramid used in fire-protective clothing.

mcq.q: UHMWPE fibres such as Dyneema are produced by:
mcq.e: Gel spinning of ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene gives high modulus fibres.

mcq.q: PTFE (Teflon) fibre is noted for its:
mcq.e: PTFE is inert to almost all chemicals.

mcq.q: PLA fibre is derived from:
mcq.e: PLA is polylactic acid from fermented starch sugars.

mcq.q: Spandex (elastane) is a:
mcq.e: Elastane is a segmented polyurethane with high stretch.

mcq.q: Electrospinning produces fibres using:
mcq.e: A high voltage draws charged polymer jets into nanofibres.

mcq.q: Silver-coated fibres are used in medical textiles mainly for their:
mcq.e: Silver ions inhibit microbial growth.

GE3252 தமிழ ரு ம் மதொழில்நுட்ப மு ம் L T P C 1 0 0 1 அலகு I மநசவு மற்றும் பொறனத் மதொழில்நுட்பம்: 3 ெங்க கொலத்தில் தநெவுத் ததொழில் – பொமனத் ததொழில்நுட்பம் - கருப்பு சிவப்பு பொண்டங்கள் – பொண்டங்களில் கீ றல் குறியீடுகள். அலகு II வடிவறமப்பு மற்றும் கட்டிடத் மதொழில்நுட்பம்: 3 ெங்க கொலத்தில் வடிவமமப்பு மற்றும் கட்டுமொனங்கள் & ெங்க கொலத்தில் வீ ட்டுப் தபொருட்களில் வடிவமமப்பு - ெங்க கொலத்தில் கட்டுமொன தபொருட்களும் நடுகல்லும் – சிலப்பதிகொரத்தில் மமமட அமமப்பு பற்றிய விவரங்கள் - மொமல்லபுரெ் சிற்பங்களும், மகொவில்களும் – மெொழர் கொலத்துப் தபருங்மகொயில்கள் மற்றும் பிற வழிபொட்டுத் தலங்கள் – நொயக்கர் கொலக் மகொயில்கள் - மொதிரி கட்டமமப்புகள் பற்றி அறிதல், மதுமர மீ னொட்சி அம்மன் ஆலயம் மற்றும் திருமமல நொயக்கர் மஹொல் – தெட்டிநொட்டு வீ டுகள் – பிரிட்டிஷ் கொலத்தில் தென்மனயில் இந்மதொ - ெொமரொதெனிக் கட்டிடக் கமல. அலகு III உற்பத்தித் மதொழில் நுட்பம்: 3 கப்பல் கட்டும் கமல – உமலொகவியல் – இரும்புத் ததொழிற்ெொமல – இரும்மப உருக்குதல், எஃகு – வரலொற்றுெ் ெொன்றுகளொக தெம்பு மற்றும் தங்க நொணயங்கள் – நொணயங்கள் அெ்ெடித்தல் – மணி உருவொக்கும் ததொழிற்ெொமலகள் – கல்மணிகள், கண்ணொடி மணிகள் – சுடுமண் மணிகள் – ெங்கு மணிகள் – எலும்புத்துண்டுகள் – ததொல்லியல் ெொன்றுகள் – சிலப்பதிகொரத்தில் மணிகளின் வமககள். அலகு IV கவளொை்றம மற்றும் நீர்ப்பொசனத் மதொழில் நுட்பம்: 3 அமண, ஏரி, குளங்கள், மதகு – மெொழர்கொலக் குமுழித் தூம்பின் முக்கியத்துவம் – கொல்நமட பரொமரிப்பு – கொல்நமடகளுக்கொக வடிவமமக்கப்பட்ட கிணறுகள் – மவளொண்மம மற்றும் மவளொண்மமெ் ெொர்ந்த தெயல்பொடுகள் – கடல்ெொர் அறிவு – மீ ன்வளம் – முத்து மற்றும் முத்துக்குளித்தல் – தபருங்கடல் குறித்த பண்மடய அறிவு – அறிவுெொர் ெமூகம். அலகு V அறிவியல் தமிழ் மற்றும் கைித்தமிழ்: 3 அறிவியல் தமிழின் வளர்ெ்சி – கணித்தமிழ் வளர்ெ்சி - தமிழ் நூல்கமள மின்பதிப்பு தெய்தல் – தமிழ் தமன்தபொருட்கள் உருவொக்கம் – தமிழ் இமணயக் கல்விக்கழகம் – தமிழ் மின் நூலகம் – இமணயத்தில் தமிழ் அகரொதிகள் – தெொற்குமவத் திட்டம். mcq.q: IR spectroscopy mainly involves which type of molecular transitions?
mcq.e: IR absorption excites molecular vibrations.

mcq.q: Beer-Lambert's law states that absorbance A = :
mcq.e: A = εcl, with ε molar absorptivity, c concentration and l path length.

mcq.q: Flame photometry is commonly used to estimate:
mcq.e: Alkali metals like Na and K emit characteristic flame colours.

mcq.q: Which microscope forms an image by electrons passing through a very thin sample?
mcq.e: TEM uses transmitted electrons through thin specimens.

mcq.q: Adsorption in which adsorbate is held by weak van der Waals forces is:
mcq.e: Physical adsorption involves weak van der Waals forces.

mcq.q: Langmuir adsorption isotherm assumes adsorption forms a:
mcq.e: Langmuir assumes monolayer coverage on uniform sites.

mcq.q: A liquid wets a solid surface well when the contact angle is:
mcq.e: Low contact angle (<90°) indicates good wetting.

mcq.q: The Freundlich isotherm is expressed as x/m = :
mcq.e: Freundlich: x/m = kP^(1/n), n > 1.

mcq.q: Temporary hardness of water is caused by:
mcq.e: Bicarbonates cause temporary hardness, removable by boiling.

mcq.q: Hardness of water is estimated by titration with:
mcq.e: EDTA complexometric titration with EBT indicator estimates hardness.

mcq.q: Reverse osmosis desalination works by applying pressure greater than:
mcq.e: RO forces water through a semipermeable membrane against osmotic pressure.

mcq.q: COD is typically determined using which oxidizing agent?
mcq.e: COD uses acidified potassium dichromate as oxidant.

mcq.q: Saponification value is the mg of KOH needed to saponify:
mcq.e: It is the mg of KOH required to saponify 1 g of fat or oil.

mcq.q: Iodine value of an oil indicates its degree of:
mcq.e: Iodine value measures the number of C=C double bonds.

mcq.q: A high viscosity index of a lubricant means its viscosity:
mcq.e: High VI oils show small viscosity change with temperature.

mcq.q: Graphite acts as a solid lubricant because of its:
o: Layered structure with weak interlayer forces
mcq.e: Weak van der Waals forces let graphite layers slide easily.

mcq.q: In dye chemistry, the group responsible for colour is the:
mcq.e: Chromophores such as -N=N- impart colour.

mcq.q: A shift of absorption to longer wavelength is called:
mcq.e: Bathochromic (red) shift moves absorption to longer wavelength.

mcq.q: Methyl orange belongs to which class of dyes?
mcq.e: Methyl orange contains the azo (-N=N-) group.

mcq.q: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acid and in base turns:
mcq.e: Phenolphthalein is pink in basic solution.
