mcq.q: Which of these is a natural protein fibre?
mcq.e: Wool is an animal keratin (protein) fibre.

mcq.q: Cotton is classified as a:
mcq.e: Cotton fibres grow on the seeds of the cotton plant.

mcq.q: X-ray diffraction of fibres is mainly used to estimate:
mcq.e: XRD patterns reveal crystalline regions and their orientation.

mcq.q: Infrared dichroism in fibres gives information on:
mcq.e: Differential absorption of polarized IR reveals molecular orientation.

mcq.q: Moisture regain is defined as the weight of water expressed as percentage of the:
mcq.e: Regain = water weight / oven-dry weight × 100.

mcq.q: Among these, which fibre has the highest moisture regain at standard conditions?
mcq.e: Wool has a regain of about 14-16%, far higher than synthetics.

mcq.q: Standard atmosphere for textile testing is:
mcq.e: Standard testing atmosphere is 65 ± 2% RH at 20 ± 2 °C (27 °C for tropical).

mcq.q: Moisture regain of a fibre at a given RH is higher when approached from:
mcq.e: Sorption hysteresis makes desorption regain higher than absorption regain.

mcq.q: Tenacity of fibres is commonly expressed in:
mcq.e: Tenacity is force per unit linear density, e.g., cN/tex.

mcq.q: Work of rupture of a fibre is the:
mcq.e: It is the area under the load-elongation curve up to break.

mcq.q: Initial modulus of a fibre is the:
o: Slope of the initial straight part of stress-strain curve
mcq.e: Initial modulus is the initial slope measuring resistance to extension.

mcq.q: With increase in humidity, the strength of cotton:
mcq.e: Cotton is stronger when wet, unlike viscose and wool.

mcq.q: Elastic recovery is the ratio of:
mcq.e: Elastic recovery = recoverable extension / total extension.

mcq.q: In extension cycling, the fibre is repeatedly taken to a fixed:
mcq.e: Extension cycling repeats stretching to the same strain level.

mcq.q: Which fibre is known for very high elastic recovery?
mcq.e: Elastane recovers almost completely from large extensions.

mcq.q: For fibres of the same material and shape, flexural rigidity varies with linear density (tex) as:
mcq.e: Flexural rigidity is proportional to E·tex^2 / density times shape factor.

mcq.q: Lustre of a fibre relates to its:
o: Reflection of light from its surface
mcq.e: Lustre is the specular reflection of light from the fibre surface.

mcq.q: Directional friction effect in wool is due to:
mcq.e: Overlapping cuticle scales give different friction against and with the scales.

mcq.q: Below the glass transition temperature Tg, a polymer fibre is:
mcq.e: Below Tg, chain segment mobility is frozen and the fibre is glassy.

mcq.q: Birefringence of a fibre is defined as:
o: Difference between refractive indices parallel and perpendicular to axis
mcq.e: Birefringence Δn = n_parallel - n_perpendicular and indicates orientation.

mcq.q: Tex is defined as the mass in grams of:
mcq.e: Tex is a direct system: grams per 1000 metres.

mcq.q: English cotton count (Ne) is the number of hanks per pound, where one hank is:
mcq.e: Ne counts 840-yard hanks in one pound; it is an indirect system.

mcq.q: A main objective of carding is to:
o: Individualise fibres and remove neps and trash
mcq.e: Carding opens tufts into individual fibres, cleans them and forms a card sliver.

mcq.q: A 20s Ne cotton yarn is approximately equal to:
The main objective of combing is to:
mcq.e: Combing removes short fibres and neps and improves parallelisation.

mcq.q: The short-fibre waste removed in combing is called:
mcq.e: Comber waste consisting of short fibres is termed noil.

mcq.q: In a rectilinear comber, the leading end of the fibre fringe held by the nippers is combed by the:
mcq.e: The half-lap cylinder combs the fringe protruding from the nippers.

mcq.q: In rectilinear combing, the trailing part of the fringe is combed when it is drawn through the:
mcq.e: During detachment the fibres are pulled through the top comb, which combs their rear ends.

mcq.q: In rotor spinning, the feed sliver is opened into individual fibres by the:
mcq.e: A toothed opening (combing) roller separates fibres before they enter the rotor.

mcq.q: Compared with ring-spun yarn of the same count, rotor yarn generally has:
mcq.e: Wrapper fibres and poor fibre orientation make rotor yarns weaker but more even.

mcq.q: DREF machines are examples of which spinning system?
mcq.e: DREF systems use perforated friction drums to twist fibres.

mcq.q: In air-jet spun yarns, strength mainly comes from:
o: Wrapper fibres around a parallel core
mcq.e: False twist leaves a largely untwisted core held by wrapper fibres.

mcq.q: The most widely used fibre for industrial sewing threads today is:
mcq.e: Polyester offers high strength, abrasion resistance and dimensional stability.

mcq.q: Gassing of cotton sewing threads is done to:
o: Remove protruding fibres and improve lustre
mcq.e: Passing through a flame burns off surface hair, giving a smooth lustrous thread.

mcq.q: A melange yarn is made by:
o: Blending fibres dyed in different colours before spinning
mcq.e: Pre-dyed fibres are blended to give a heather/melange effect.

mcq.q: False-twist texturing is applicable mainly to:
mcq.e: Heat-setting in twisted state and untwisting gives bulk only in thermoplastic filaments.

mcq.q: Which fibres are typically produced by melt spinning?
mcq.e: Polymers that melt without decomposing, like PET and nylon, are melt spun.

mcq.q: Cellulose acetate fibres are commonly produced by:
mcq.e: Acetate dissolved in acetone is extruded and the solvent evaporates in hot air.

mcq.q: Electrospinning is mainly used to produce:
mcq.e: A high-voltage field draws polymer solution into very fine nanoscale fibres.

mcq.q: Thermotropic liquid-crystal polymers form an ordered liquid-crystalline phase:
o: Only when dissolved in a solvent
In the melt within a temperature range
mcq.e: Thermotropic LCPs show mesophase in the melt, enabling high-orientation fibres like Vectran.

mcq.q: In a woven fabric, warp yarns run:
mcq.e: Warp yarns are the lengthwise threads; weft runs across.

mcq.q: Pirn winding prepares yarn for use as:
mcq.e: Pirns carry weft yarn inside the shuttle.

mcq.q: The main object of sizing warp yarn is to:
o: Improve strength and abrasion resistance during weaving
mcq.e: Size coats the yarn and lays hairs to withstand loom stresses.

mcq.q: Denting refers to passing warp ends through the:
mcq.e: Denting places warp ends in the reed dents, after drawing-in through healds.

mcq.q: The primary motions of weaving are:
mcq.e: Shedding, picking and beat-up are essential to interlace yarns.

mcq.q: Take-up and let-off are classified as:
mcq.e: They control fabric winding and warp delivery for continuous weaving.

mcq.q: The weft stop motion of a loom is classified as a(n):
mcq.e: It stops the loom on weft breakage and is an auxiliary motion.

mcq.q: A loom runs at 200 picks/min but inserts 9600 picks per hour. Its efficiency is:
mcq.e: Theoretical picks = 200 x 60 = 12000, and 9600/12000 = 80%.

mcq.q: Compared with tappet shedding, a dobby is used to:
o: Control a larger number of heald shafts
mcq.e: Dobbies handle more heald shafts, allowing larger design repeats.

mcq.q: In a projectile loom, the weft is inserted by:
mcq.e: A small gripper projectile carries the weft through the shed.

mcq.q: In the 4-point fabric inspection system, the maximum penalty points assigned to a single defect is:
mcq.e: Defects are scored 1 to 4 points by length; 4 is the maximum.

mcq.q: In a double rapier loom, the weft is transferred from the giver to the taker rapier at the:
mcq.e: Two rapiers meet mid-width and the weft passes between them.

mcq.q: In a knitted fabric, a wale is a:
mcq.e: Wales run lengthwise; courses run widthwise.

mcq.q: Which knitting needle has a pivoting latch that closes the hook by itself?
mcq.e: The latch is self-acting, closed and opened by the loop movement.

mcq.q: A bearded needle requires which element to close its beard during knitting?
mcq.e: The flexible beard is closed by a presser.

mcq.q: A single jersey circular machine of 30 inch diameter and 24 gauge has about how many needles?
mcq.e: Needles = π x diameter x gauge = 3.1416 x 30 x 24 ≈ 2262.

mcq.q: Needle punching is a method of:
mcq.e: Barbed needles entangle fibres mechanically.

mcq.q: In spun bonding, the web is formed from:
o: Continuous filaments extruded and laid directly
mcq.e: Polymer is extruded into filaments that are laid as a web directly.

mcq.q: The melt blown process is known for producing:
mcq.e: Hot high-velocity air attenuates molten polymer into microfibres.

mcq.q: Bonding of a nonwoven web by high-pressure water jets is called:
mcq.e: Water jets entangle fibres in spunlace bonding.

mcq.q: The minimum repeat of a plain weave is:
mcq.e: Plain weave interlaces alternately, repeating on 2 ends and 2 picks.

mcq.q: The characteristic feature of a twill weave is:
mcq.e: Twill produces diagonal ribs by stepping the interlacing.

mcq.q: The minimum number of ends in a regular sateen/satin repeat is:
mcq.e: Regular satins need at least 5 threads; 4-end satins are irregular.

mcq.q: A peg plan indicates:
o: The order of drawing ends into healds
The lifting order of heald shafts
mcq.e: The draft shows drawing-in; the peg plan shows which shafts lift on each pick.

mcq.q: A double cloth is made with:
o: Two sets of warp and two sets of weft
mcq.e: Two complete fabric layers are woven together using two warps and two wefts.

mcq.q: Plain face Bedford cord produces cords running in which direction?
mcq.e: Bedford cords are longitudinal cords; welts or piques run weftway.

mcq.q: The main purpose of warp or weft backed fabrics is to:
o: Increase weight and warmth without changing the face
mcq.e: An extra series on the back adds weight and bulk while the face remains unchanged.

mcq.q: In interchanging plain double cloth, the figure is produced by:
mcq.e: Face and back layers interchange to create the design.

mcq.q: Terry pile fabrics commonly used for towels are which type of pile?
mcq.e: Terry is a warp pile with uncut loops formed by a pile warp.

mcq.q: Corduroy is classified as a:
mcq.e: Corduroy pile is formed by cutting weft floats.

mcq.q: Leno fabrics are characterised by:
mcq.e: In leno, doup ends cross over standard ends, locking the weft.

mcq.q: The main difference of a Jacquard over a dobby is that a Jacquard controls:
mcq.e: Jacquards lift warp ends individually, enabling large figured designs.

mcq.q: In knitting, a wale is:
mcq.e: A wale runs lengthwise; a course runs across.

mcq.q: Single jersey fabric is knitted on:
o: Two needle beds in rib gating
mcq.e: Single jersey uses a single set of needles.

mcq.q: Interlock fabric can be described as:
mcq.e: Interlock combines two 1x1 ribs, looking like face loops on both sides.

mcq.q: Half cardigan and full cardigan are rib derivatives that use which stitch?
mcq.e: Cardigan structures add tucks on one bed (half) or alternately on both beds (full).

mcq.q: In warp knitting, loops are formed:
o: Across the width from one yarn
Lengthwise, each needle fed by its own yarn
mcq.e: Warp knitting uses a warp sheet with guides lapping yarn onto every needle.

mcq.q: A pillar (chain) stitch in warp knitting is formed when a guide:
o: Laps the same needle every course
mcq.e: Lapping the same needle each course forms separate chains of loops.

mcq.q: Compared with weft knits, warp knit fabrics are generally:
mcq.e: Interlinking of laps from multiple guide bars reduces laddering.

mcq.q: The two main classes of warp knitting machines are:
mcq.e: Tricot and Raschel are the main warp knitting machine types.

mcq.q: A motif based on flowers and leaves is classified as:
mcq.e: Motifs derived from plants and animals are natural forms.

mcq.q: Which motif arrangement places a motif in each repeat moved halfway down beside the previous column?
mcq.e: In half drop arrangement alternate columns are shifted by half the repeat.

mcq.q: Garment design that adds trims and ornamentation to the surface is:
mcq.e: Decorative design applies embellishments to the garment's surface.

mcq.q: The ogee base is a framework shaped like:
mcq.e: Ogee is a double curve forming onion-shaped compartments.

mcq.q: Which of these is an element of design?
mcq.e: Line is an element; balance, rhythm and emphasis are principles.

mcq.q: The name of a colour such as red or blue is its:
mcq.e: Hue is the name of a colour family.

mcq.q: Lightness or darkness of a colour is its:
mcq.e: Value describes how light or dark a colour is.

mcq.q: Colours opposite each other on the colour wheel form a:
mcq.e: Complementary colours lie directly opposite on the wheel.

mcq.q: Haute couture refers to:
mcq.e: Haute couture is made-to-order high fashion from exclusive houses.

mcq.q: The correct order of the fashion life cycle is:
mcq.e: Fashions are introduced, rise, peak (culminate), decline and become obsolete.

mcq.q: The trickle-down theory states fashion moves from:
mcq.e: Trickle-down theory says fashion starts with elites and is copied by lower classes.

mcq.q: A fad is a fashion that:
mcq.e: A fad gains quick popularity and fades rapidly.

mcq.q: The main textile used in ancient Egyptian garments was:
mcq.e: Egyptians wore linen made from flax.

mcq.q: The chiton was a garment of ancient:
mcq.e: The chiton was a draped tunic worn in ancient Greece.

mcq.q: The 'mundu' is a traditional garment of:
mcq.e: The mundu is the traditional wrap worn in Kerala.

mcq.q: The phanek is a traditional wrap-around garment of women in:
mcq.e: Manipuri women wear the phanek, a sarong-like garment.

mcq.q: Kanchipuram silk saris are woven in the state of:
mcq.e: Kanchipuram is in Tamil Nadu.

mcq.q: Phulkari embroidery belongs to:
mcq.e: Phulkari ('flower work') is the embroidery of Punjab.

mcq.q: Paithani saris originate from:
mcq.e: Paithani saris come from Paithan in Maharashtra.

mcq.q: Kalamkari is a hand-painted / block-printed textile from:
mcq.e: Kalamkari is associated with Andhra Pradesh, e.g. Srikalahasti and Machilipatnam.

mcq.q: Marker efficiency is the ratio of:
o: Area of pattern pieces to total marker area
mcq.e: Efficiency (%) = pattern area / marker area x 100.

mcq.q: Fabrics with nap or pile that must be spread with all plies facing one direction are called:
mcq.e: Directional fabrics like velvet require one-way spreading.

mcq.q: Face-to-face spreading in zig-zag form is suitable for:
mcq.e: Zig-zag spreading suits non-directional fabrics.

mcq.q: The 4-point system is used for:
mcq.e: Defects are scored 1-4 points based on length in fabric inspection.

mcq.q: The most widely used cutting machine in garment industry for cutting lays is the:
mcq.e: Straight knife machines are versatile for high lays.

mcq.q: Round knife cutting machines are best for:
mcq.e: Round knives cut straight and gentle curves in low lays.

mcq.q: Band knife cutting machines are preferred for:
mcq.e: The blade passes through a fixed slot, giving high accuracy for small parts.

mcq.q: A computerised cutting system holds the lay firmly using:
o: Vacuum suction under a polythene cover
mcq.e: CAD cutters compress the lay with vacuum under a plastic film.

mcq.q: The part that moves fabric forward after each stitch is the:
mcq.e: The feed dog teeth advance the fabric.

mcq.q: A lockstitch machine forms stitch class:
mcq.e: Lockstitch is ISO stitch type 301.

mcq.q: The take-up lever in a sewing machine:
o: Pulls up slack thread to set the stitch
mcq.e: It supplies and withdraws needle thread to tighten the stitch.

mcq.q: The groove on the needle that guides thread during penetration is the:
mcq.e: The long groove protects the thread as the needle penetrates.

mcq.q: Overlock machines are mainly used for:
mcq.e: Overlock trims and covers edges to prevent fraying.

mcq.q: In an overlock machine, a differential feed ratio greater than 1 produces:
mcq.e: Front feed moving faster than rear feed gathers the fabric.

mcq.q: In overlock stitching, the threads that form loops on the fabric edge are supplied by:
mcq.e: Upper and lower loopers carry threads around the edge.

mcq.q: The ISO stitch class for 3-thread overlock is:
mcq.e: 504 is the standard 3-thread overedge stitch.

mcq.q: A buttonhole machine primarily produces stitches of type:
mcq.e: Buttonholes are formed by dense zig-zag lockstitch.

mcq.q: The feed-off-the-arm machine is used to sew:
o: Tubular items like side seams of jeans
mcq.e: Fabric is fed off a cylindrical arm for closing tubular seams.

mcq.q: A zig-zag machine produces a stitch where the needle moves:
mcq.e: Lateral needle movement creates the zig-zag pattern.

mcq.q: A key merit of computerized sewing machines is:
mcq.e: Microprocessor control enables stored patterns and repeatable quality.

mcq.q: GSM in fabric testing stands for:
mcq.e: GSM is the areal density of fabric in g/m^2.

mcq.q: Moisture regain is the weight of moisture expressed as a percentage of:
mcq.e: Regain = moisture weight/dry weight × 100.

mcq.q: The international standard atmosphere for textile testing (ISO 139) is 65% RH at a temperature of:
mcq.e: ISO 139 specifies 65 ± 4% RH at 20 ± 2 °C for conditioning and testing.

mcq.q: A fabric with moisture regain 10% has moisture content of about:
The grab test is used to measure fabric:
mcq.e: The grab test measures tensile (breaking) strength.

mcq.q: The Elmendorf tester measures:
mcq.e: Elmendorf uses a falling pendulum to measure tear strength.

mcq.q: Bursting strength tests are especially suitable for:
mcq.e: Knits are tested for bursting strength as they stretch in all directions.

mcq.q: In a ravelled strip test, the strip width is obtained by:
mcq.e: Yarns are ravelled from both sides to get the exact test width.

mcq.q: Fabric drape is quantified by the:
mcq.e: Drape coefficient measures how a fabric hangs.

mcq.q: Flexural rigidity is commonly measured with the:
mcq.e: The cantilever stiffness tester gives bending length and flexural rigidity.

mcq.q: The Martindale tester is used for assessing:
mcq.e: Martindale abrades fabric in a Lissajous pattern to assess abrasion and pilling.

mcq.q: Colour fastness to light is assessed using:
mcq.e: Light fastness is rated against blue wool reference standards.

mcq.q: KES-F stands for:
mcq.e: KES-F measures low-stress mechanical properties.

mcq.q: FAST was developed by:
mcq.e: FAST (Fabric Assurance by Simple Testing) was developed by CSIRO.

mcq.q: In KES-F, the instrument KES-FB1 measures:
mcq.e: KES-FB1 measures tensile and shear; FB2 bending, FB3 compression, FB4 surface.

mcq.q: Low-stress mechanical properties of fabrics mainly relate to:
mcq.e: Low-stress properties determine fabric hand and tailorability.

mcq.q: In the 4-point system, the maximum penalty points for a single defect are:
mcq.e: Defects over 9 inches receive the maximum 4 points.

mcq.q: In the 10-point system, a defect of length up to 1 inch gets:
mcq.e: Defects up to 1 inch are penalised 1 point in the 10-point system.

mcq.q: AQL stands for:
mcq.e: AQL is the acceptable quality level used in sampling inspection.

mcq.q: Twisting of a knitted garment's side seam toward front or back is called:
mcq.e: Spirality is the skewing of wales in knitted fabrics and garments.

mcq.q: The first sample made to check the style and design interpretation of a garment is the:
mcq.e: The proto sample is the first prototype used to evaluate design, fit and construction.

mcq.q: The sample made with actual bulk fabric and trims and approved just before bulk production is the:
mcq.e: The PP sample confirms materials and construction before bulk production begins.

mcq.q: Pattern grading refers to:
o: Producing patterns in different sizes from a base size
Laying fabric plies on the table
mcq.e: Grading scales the base pattern up and down to create a full size range.

mcq.q: The sample produced in all sizes to check grading and fit before production is the:
mcq.e: Size set samples are made across the size range to verify graded patterns and measurements.

mcq.q: Hook and loop fasteners are commonly known by the trade name:
mcq.e: Velcro is the popular trade name for hook and loop fastening tape.

mcq.q: Interlinings are used in garments mainly to:
o: Provide shape and support to parts like collars and cuffs
mcq.e: Interlinings add body, stiffness and shape retention to garment components.

mcq.q: In the Tex system of thread numbering, a higher Tex number indicates a:
mcq.e: Tex is the mass in grams of 1000 m of thread, so a larger Tex means a heavier, coarser thread.

mcq.q: ISO 4915 stitch type 301 is the:
mcq.e: Stitch class 300 is lockstitch, and 301 is the plain lockstitch used on most sewing machines.

mcq.q: Marker efficiency is calculated as:
o: (Area of pattern pieces / Area of marker) × 100
(Area of marker / Area of pattern pieces) × 100
Number of pieces / Number of plies
mcq.e: Marker efficiency is the percentage of marker area actually used by pattern pieces.

mcq.q: The lengthwise grain of a woven fabric runs parallel to the:
mcq.e: Warp yarns run along the length of the fabric, parallel to the selvedge.

mcq.q: The true bias of a woven fabric is at what angle to the warp?
mcq.e: True bias lies at 45° to both warp and weft and gives maximum stretch.

mcq.q: In the 4-point fabric inspection system, the maximum penalty points assigned to any single defect is:
mcq.e: Defects are scored 1 to 4 points by length, so no single defect receives more than 4 points.
mcq.t: Objectives and requirements of fabric inspection

mcq.q: The Unit Production System (UPS) transports garment components using:
o: Bundles tied and moved on trolleys
Operators carrying full garments by hand
No transport since one person makes the garment
An overhead hanger conveyor carrying individual garments
mcq.e: UPS uses an overhead rail with hangers that move one garment's pieces between workstations.

mcq.q: A modular production system uses:
o: One operator per operation in a long line
A small team of multi-skilled, cross-trained operators
mcq.e: In modular systems a team of cross-trained operators completes the garment, often in standing work.

mcq.q: In which production system does one operator assemble the entire garment?
mcq.e: In the make-through or individual system, a single operator performs all operations.

mcq.q: Work-in-progress (WIP) inventory is typically the highest in the:
mcq.e: PBS keeps large bundles waiting between operations to balance the line, leading to high WIP.

mcq.q: The three main parameters controlled in fusing are:
mcq.e: Proper fusing depends on the correct combination of temperature, pressure and dwell time.

mcq.q: Polybags in garment packaging mainly serve to:
o: Protect the garment from dust, soiling and moisture
mcq.e: Polybags provide a clean protective cover during handling, storage and transport.

mcq.q: The vacuum in a garment pressing table is used to:
o: Remove moisture and set the garment
mcq.e: Vacuum draws out steam and moisture, cooling the fabric so the pressed shape is set.

mcq.q: Using too high a fusing temperature can cause:
o: Insufficient resin melting and poor bond
Resin strike-through to the face of the fabric
mcq.e: Excess heat makes the adhesive too fluid so it penetrates through to the outer fabric surface.

mcq.q: In the eight head theory, the ideal adult figure height equals:
mcq.e: The ideal fashion proportion uses eight head lengths for total height.

mcq.q: Anthropometry is the study of:
mcq.e: Anthropometry measures human body dimensions.

mcq.q: For a women's bodice, the bust measurement is taken:
o: Around the fullest part of the bust
mcq.e: Bust girth is measured horizontally over the fullest part.

mcq.q: A sizing system mainly helps to:
o: Fit a large population with a limited set of sizes
mcq.e: Sizing systems group body dimensions into standard sizes.

mcq.q: Draping is a pattern making method in which fabric is:
o: Shaped directly on a dress form
mcq.e: Draping manipulates fabric directly on a form.

mcq.q: The line indicating the direction of the warp on a pattern is the:
mcq.e: Grainline is aligned with the fabric's lengthwise grain.

mcq.q: Notches on a pattern are used to:
mcq.e: Notches help align corresponding pieces.

mcq.q: A basic block (sloper) is a:
o: Fitted foundation pattern without style lines
mcq.e: Slopers are basic fitted patterns used to develop styles.

mcq.q: Pattern grading is the process of:
o: Changing pattern size up or down
mcq.e: Grading creates patterns in multiple sizes from a base size.

mcq.q: Grade rules specify:
o: Amount and direction of increment at each point
mcq.e: Grade rules define x-y movement of pattern points between sizes.

mcq.q: Lengthening a bodice pattern is generally done by:
o: Slashing and spreading at the lengthen/shorten line
Adding a dart at the neck
mcq.e: Patterns are cut and spread parallel at the alteration line.

mcq.q: Grading done by cutting a pattern and spreading the pieces by grade amounts is called:
mcq.e: Cut-and-spread grading slashes the pattern and spreads pieces.

mcq.q: The point of a dart pointing toward the bust is called the:
mcq.e: Dart point is the tip towards the fullest area.

mcq.q: In the pivotal transfer technique, the pattern is pivoted around the:
mcq.e: Pivoting at the bust point transfers the dart to a new position.

mcq.q: In slash-and-spread dart manipulation, the original dart is:
o: Closed and a new dart opens at the slash
mcq.e: Closing the original dart opens the intake at the slashed location.

mcq.q: Radiating darts in a bodice are darts that:
o: Emanate from a common point such as the bust point
mcq.e: Radiating darts spread outward from one point, usually the bust point.

mcq.q: A Peter Pan collar is a:
mcq.e: Peter Pan collars lie flat with rounded front edges.

mcq.q: A mandarin collar is a:
mcq.e: Mandarin collars stand up around the neck without a fall.

mcq.q: A sailor collar is characterized by a:
mcq.e: The sailor collar has a large square flap at the back and V neckline.

mcq.q: A leg-of-mutton sleeve is:
o: Fitted at top, flared at wrist
Full and puffed at the top, fitted at the wrist
mcq.e: It is wide at the upper arm and tapers to a fitted forearm.

mcq.q: Enzymatic desizing of starch-sized cotton uses:
mcq.e: Amylase hydrolyses starch into soluble sugars that are washed out.

mcq.q: A commonly used stabiliser in hydrogen peroxide bleaching of cotton is:
mcq.e: Sodium silicate controls peroxide decomposition and buffers the alkaline bath.

mcq.q: Mercerisation of cotton is carried out using concentrated:
mcq.e: Strong caustic soda swells cotton, increasing lustre, strength and dye uptake.

mcq.q: Optical brightening agents whiten fabric by:
o: Absorbing UV light and emitting blue light
mcq.e: Fluorescence in the blue region masks yellowness.

mcq.q: Reactive dyes are fixed on cotton by forming:
mcq.e: Reactive groups react with cellulose hydroxyl groups to form covalent bonds.

mcq.q: Vat dyes are applied to cotton in their:
mcq.e: Vat dyes are reduced in alkali to a soluble leuco form, absorbed, then reoxidised.

mcq.q: High-temperature high-pressure dyeing of polyester with disperse dyes is done at about:
mcq.e: At around 130 C polyester chains open up enough for disperse dyes to diffuse.

mcq.q: In thermosol dyeing of polyester, the padded fabric is heated at about:
mcq.e: Dry heat around 200-220 C for about a minute fixes disperse dyes.

mcq.q: The main function of a thickener in print paste is to:
mcq.e: Thickeners give sharp prints by holding dye in place.

mcq.q: In batik printing, the resist material used is:
mcq.e: Hot wax applied to fabric resists dye penetration in those areas.

mcq.q: Rotary screen printing uses:
o: Flat silk screens moved by hand
mcq.e: Electroformed nickel cylinders rotate with paste fed from inside.

mcq.q: A common discharging agent used in discharge printing of cellulosics is:
mcq.e: Rongalite (sodium formaldehyde sulphoxylate) destroys the ground dye in printed areas.

mcq.q: Calendering gives fabric a smooth lustrous surface by:
o: Passing it between heated rollers under pressure
mcq.e: Heat and pressure flatten yarns and increase surface lustre.

mcq.q: Stone washing of denim traditionally uses:
mcq.e: Pumice abrades the indigo-dyed surface to give a faded look.

mcq.q: Bio-polishing of cotton fabrics is done using:
mcq.e: Cellulase removes protruding microfibrils, reducing fuzz and pilling.

mcq.q: Crease-resist finishes such as DMDHEU work on cotton mainly by:
mcq.e: Crosslinks restrict chain slippage so the fabric recovers from creasing.

mcq.q: The visible range of the electromagnetic spectrum is approximately:
mcq.e: Human vision responds roughly between 400 and 700 nm.

mcq.q: The Kubelka-Munk function used for colour strength is:
mcq.e: K/S relates reflectance R to absorption K and scattering S of the dyed substrate.

mcq.q: For a reflectance R = 0.5, the Kubelka-Munk value K/S is:
In the CIELAB system, the L* coordinate represents:
mcq.e: L* runs from 0 (black) to 100 (white); a* and b* are the chromatic axes.

mcq.q: A patch pocket is a pocket that is:
o: Stitched onto the outside surface of the garment
mcq.e: Patch pockets are separate pieces sewn on the outside.

mcq.q: Facings are used on necklines and armholes mainly to:
mcq.e: Facings finish and support cut edges like necklines.

mcq.q: A welt pocket is classified as a(n):
mcq.e: It is set into a slit in the garment and finished with a welt.

mcq.q: In an inverted box pleat, the two folds:
o: Face away from each other on the outside
Meet at the centre on the outside
mcq.e: Inverted pleats have folds meeting at the centre on the right side.

mcq.q: A romper for children is a:
o: One-piece garment combining top and shorts
mcq.e: Rompers join the top and short pants in one piece.

mcq.q: Fabrics preferred for infants' wear are generally:
mcq.e: Infant skin needs soft, breathable, absorbent fabrics.

mcq.q: Operation breakdown of a garment means:
o: Listing the sequence of operations to assemble it
mcq.e: It lists each sewing operation in order for production planning.

mcq.q: For young children's garments, drawstrings at the hood and neck are avoided mainly because of:
mcq.e: Neck drawstrings can catch and choke children.

mcq.q: In a men's shirt, the yoke is the:
o: Shaped piece across the back shoulders
mcq.e: The yoke joins back and shoulders, supporting the shirt.

mcq.q: Jeans are traditionally made from:
mcq.e: Denim is the classic heavy cotton fabric for jeans.

mcq.q: The small extra pocket inside the front right pocket of five-pocket jeans is the:
mcq.e: It was originally for a pocket watch, now called the coin pocket.

mcq.q: Classic denim for jeans is usually woven as a:
mcq.e: Denim is typically a 3/1 twill with dyed warp.

mcq.q: In a raglan sleeve, the seam runs:
o: Down the centre of the sleeve
Diagonally from the underarm to the neckline
mcq.e: Raglan seams extend from underarm to neck, merging sleeve and shoulder.

mcq.q: A tank top is a:
mcq.e: Tank tops are sleeveless with shoulder straps.

mcq.q: A princess line garment shapes the body with:
mcq.e: Long vertical seams over the bust incorporate dart shaping.

mcq.q: Bias cut dresses are cut with the grain at an angle of:
mcq.e: True bias is 45° to the lengthwise grain, giving drape and stretch.

mcq.q: A camisole is:
o: A sleeveless undergarment with thin straps
mcq.e: Camisoles are light sleeveless tops worn as lingerie or under clothes.

mcq.q: In India, a petticoat is commonly worn:
mcq.e: The saree is tucked into the waistband of the petticoat.

mcq.q: An A-line skirt is:
o: Fitted at the waist and flaring gradually to the hem
mcq.e: Its outline resembles the letter A.

mcq.q: Brassiere cup size is determined from the difference between:
mcq.e: Cup size reflects how much bust exceeds the band measurement.

mcq.q: Concurrent engineering in garment manufacturing means:
o: Performing tasks strictly one after another
Carrying out design and production activities in parallel
mcq.e: Concurrent engineering overlaps product and process development to save time.

mcq.q: Reverse engineering of a garment involves:
o: Analysing an existing garment to derive its specifications
mcq.e: Studying a finished garment reveals patterns, construction and specs.

mcq.q: A time and action (T&A) calendar is used to:
o: Schedule critical activities from order to shipment
mcq.e: The T&A calendar tracks key milestones against deadlines.

mcq.q: Which sample is approved just before bulk production starts?
mcq.e: The PP sample confirms materials and construction before bulk.

mcq.q: A marker of area 10 m^2 contains pattern pieces of total area 8.5 m^2. Marker efficiency is:
mcq.e: Efficiency = 8.5/10 x 100 = 85%.

mcq.q: For one-way fabrics such as napped or directional prints, patterns must be:
o: Placed all in the same direction
mcq.e: Directional fabrics need uniform orientation, usually lowering marker efficiency.
mcq.t: Influence of fabric design on marker making

mcq.q: The purpose of bundling cut pieces with tickets is to:
o: Track pieces and keep size and shade together
mcq.e: Bundle tickets keep related parts together and allow tracking through sewing.

mcq.q: In lay planning, the number of plies is mainly determined by:
o: Order quantity by size and colour
mcq.e: Plies and marker ratios are planned to meet ordered quantities per size and colour.

mcq.q: Line balancing aims to:
o: Distribute work so workstation loads are nearly equal
mcq.e: Balancing equalises workloads to maximise flow and output.

mcq.q: A bottleneck operation in a sewing line is the one with:
o: The highest work content per operator (lowest capacity)
mcq.e: The slowest station limits line output.

mcq.q: SAM 15 min, target 800 pieces per 480-minute day at 100% efficiency. Operators needed:
mcq.e: Operators = 15 x 800 / 480 = 25.

mcq.q: An operation breakdown lists:
o: Each sewing operation in sequence with machine type and SAM
mcq.e: It is the basis for layout, machinery allocation and line balancing.
mcq.t: Operation break down and production sequence

mcq.q: The main aim of JIT production is to:
o: Minimise inventory by producing only what is needed when needed
mcq.e: JIT reduces waste by synchronising production with demand.

mcq.q: A Kanban system works as a:
mcq.e: Kanban cards signal downstream demand to pull material.

mcq.q: With annual demand 800 units, ordering cost Rs 100 per order, holding cost Rs 4 per unit per year, EOQ is:
VED analysis classifies inventory items according to:
mcq.e: VED ranks items by how critical they are to production; ABC ranks by value.

mcq.q: AQL stands for:
mcq.e: AQL is the maximum defect level accepted as a satisfactory process average.

mcq.q: Solid packing means each carton contains garments of:
mcq.e: Solid pack is single size and colour per carton, unlike ratio packing.

o: Shipping a quantity less than the ordered quantity
Shipping by air instead of sea
mcq.e: Short shipment means the delivered quantity falls short of the order.

mcq.q: Dividing consumers into groups based on age, income and gender is called:
mcq.e: Age, income and gender are demographic variables.

mcq.q: Segmentation based on lifestyle, values and personality is:
mcq.e: Psychographic segmentation uses lifestyle and personality traits.

mcq.q: Ready-to-wear fashion is also known as:
mcq.e: Prêt-à-porter is French for ready-to-wear.

mcq.q: The first stage of the consumer buying decision process is:
mcq.e: The process begins when a consumer recognizes a need.

mcq.q: The 4 Ps of the marketing mix are:
mcq.e: The classic marketing mix is product, price, place and promotion.

mcq.q: Brand positioning refers to:
o: The distinct place a brand occupies in the customer's mind
The shelf location of a product
mcq.e: Positioning defines how a brand is perceived relative to competitors.

mcq.q: Selling fabric to a garment manufacturer is an example of:
mcq.e: Sales between businesses form the business-to-business market.

mcq.q: SWOT analysis evaluates:
mcq.e: SWOT covers internal strengths/weaknesses and external opportunities/threats.

mcq.q: The 'five rights' of merchandising include the right product at the right:
mcq.e: Merchandising delivers the right product, place, time, quantity and price.

mcq.q: A group of related products offered together under one category is a:
mcq.e: A product line is a group of related items, e.g. men's shirts.

mcq.q: The cost sheet in apparel costing includes fabric, trims, CMT and:
mcq.e: Garment cost includes materials, CMT, overheads and margin.

mcq.q: CMT in apparel merchandising stands for:
mcq.e: CMT is the cost of cutting, making and trimming a garment.

mcq.q: Sourcing in apparel refers to:
o: Finding and procuring materials and manufacturers
mcq.e: Sourcing identifies suppliers for materials and production.

mcq.q: ERP stands for:
mcq.e: ERP integrates business processes across an enterprise.

mcq.q: Quick Response (QR) strategy aims to:
o: Shorten lead times by sharing data across the supply chain
mcq.e: QR reduces lead time and inventory through supply chain collaboration.

mcq.q: Sourcing production from a nearby country to reduce lead time is called:
mcq.e: Near-shoring locates sourcing close to the target market.

mcq.q: A letter of credit is issued by the:
mcq.e: The importer's bank issues an LC guaranteeing payment to the exporter.

mcq.q: The document issued by a carrier acknowledging receipt of goods for sea shipment is the:
mcq.e: A bill of lading is the carrier's receipt and document of title.

mcq.q: A certificate of origin certifies:
o: The country where goods were manufactured
mcq.e: It states the country of origin of the exported goods.

mcq.q: Under FOB terms, risk passes from seller to buyer when goods:
o: Are loaded on board the vessel at the port of shipment
mcq.e: FOB transfers risk once goods are on board the vessel.

mcq.q: The law of demand states that, other things equal, quantity demanded:
mcq.e: Demand varies inversely with price.

mcq.q: A market with a single seller and no close substitutes is:
mcq.e: A monopoly has one seller.

mcq.q: Under perfect competition, the firm's price equals:
mcq.e: For a price-taker, P = AR = MR.

mcq.q: Equilibrium price is determined where:
mcq.e: Market equilibrium occurs where quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

mcq.q: The Phillips curve shows the relationship between:
mcq.e: The Phillips curve shows an inverse relation between inflation and unemployment.

mcq.q: Monetary policy in India is conducted by the:
mcq.e: The RBI formulates and implements monetary policy.

mcq.q: Inflation caused by rising production costs such as wages and raw materials is:
mcq.e: Cost-push inflation arises from increased input costs.

mcq.q: Fiscal policy relates to government decisions on:
mcq.e: Fiscal policy concerns taxation and government spending.

mcq.q: Prime cost is the sum of direct material, direct labour and:
mcq.e: Prime cost = direct material + direct labour + direct expenses.

mcq.q: Break-even point (units) equals fixed cost divided by:
mcq.e: BEP = Fixed cost/(Selling price - Variable cost per unit).

mcq.q: Fixed cost ₹50,000, price ₹100/unit, variable cost ₹60/unit. BEP is:
The P/V ratio is defined as:
mcq.e: P/V ratio = contribution/sales × 100.

mcq.q: Overheads are costs that:
o: Cannot be directly traced to a specific product
mcq.e: Overheads are indirect costs apportioned to products.

mcq.q: Fabric cost per garment mainly depends on fabric price and:
mcq.e: Fabric cost = consumption per garment × price per unit length/weight.

mcq.q: In India, GST was introduced in the year:
mcq.e: GST was implemented from 1 July 2017.

mcq.q: Distributing overheads to cost centres on a suitable basis is called:
mcq.e: Apportionment distributes common overheads over cost centres.

mcq.q: Forward contracts in foreign exchange are used mainly to:
mcq.e: Forward contracts lock in exchange rates to reduce risk.

mcq.q: If the rupee depreciates against the US dollar, an Indian apparel exporter earns:
o: More rupees per dollar of sales
mcq.e: Depreciation means each dollar converts into more rupees.

mcq.q: A budget that adjusts to different levels of activity is a:
mcq.e: A flexible budget is prepared for various activity levels.

mcq.q: The budget that integrates all functional budgets of an organization is the:
mcq.e: The master budget summarises all functional budgets.

mcq.q: The term scramjet stands for:
mcq.e: In a scramjet the flow remains supersonic through the combustor.

mcq.q: At high hypersonic Mach numbers, a ramjet with subsonic combustion becomes inefficient mainly because:
o: There is insufficient oxygen in air
Decelerating flow to subsonic speed causes excessive temperature and losses
mcq.e: Strong shocks to reach subsonic speed cause large stagnation pressure losses and very high static temperatures with dissociation.

mcq.q: Compression in a scramjet engine is achieved by:
o: Ram compression through the inlet shock system
mcq.e: Scramjets have no rotating machinery; the inlet geometry and shocks compress the air.

mcq.q: Hydrogen is attractive as a scramjet fuel mainly because of its:
o: Very fast reaction kinetics and high heat release per kg
mcq.e: Residence time in the combustor is only milliseconds, so hydrogen's fast kinetics and high energy content are essential.

mcq.q: Specific impulse (in seconds) is defined as:
mcq.e: Isp is thrust per unit weight flow rate of propellant, F/(ṁ g0).
mcq.t: Prediction and Measurement of Specific Impulse

mcq.q: The burning rate law for solid propellants (Saint Robert's law) is:
mcq.e: The burn rate varies with chamber pressure as r = a p^n.

mcq.q: A grain whose burning surface area increases with time gives:
mcq.e: Increasing burning area raises mass generation and chamber pressure, which is progressive burning.

mcq.q: For stable operation of a solid rocket motor, the pressure exponent n in r = a p^n must be:
mcq.e: With n < 1, a pressure rise increases nozzle outflow faster than gas generation, restoring equilibrium.

mcq.q: Hypergolic propellants are those that:
o: Ignite spontaneously on contact with each other
Need a spark plug for ignition
mcq.e: Hypergolic fuel and oxidizer ignite immediately when they mix, e.g. MMH and N2O4.

mcq.q: Which of the following is a cryogenic bipropellant combination?
mcq.e: Both liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen are stored at cryogenic temperatures.

mcq.q: Gas pressure feed systems are usually preferred for:
o: Low-thrust engines such as reaction control thrusters
mcq.e: Pressure-fed systems need heavy high-pressure tanks, so they suit small, low-thrust engines.

mcq.q: In which engine cycle is the turbine exhaust injected into the main combustion chamber?
mcq.e: In staged combustion the preburner gas drives the turbine and then enters the main chamber, unlike the open gas generator cycle.
mcq.t: Turbo pump Feed Systems and Engine Cycles

mcq.q: A typical hybrid rocket uses:
o: A liquid fuel and a liquid oxidizer
A premixed solid fuel and solid oxidizer
A solid fuel and a liquid oxidizer
mcq.e: Classical hybrids burn a solid fuel grain with a liquid or gaseous oxidizer.

mcq.q: A commonly used solid fuel in hybrid rocket motors is:
mcq.e: Hydroxyl-terminated polybutadiene (HTPB) is a widely used hybrid fuel grain.

mcq.q: In a classical hybrid motor, the fuel regression rate is commonly expressed as:
mcq.e: Hybrid regression is governed by convective heat transfer, correlated with oxidizer mass flux Gox.

mcq.q: The O/F shift in a hybrid rocket during a burn is caused mainly by:
o: Change in port geometry as the fuel regresses
mcq.e: As the port enlarges, oxidizer flux and burning area change, so fuel flow and O/F vary at constant oxidizer flow.

mcq.q: The most commonly used propellant in modern ion thrusters is:
mcq.e: Xenon is heavy, inert and easily ionized, making it ideal for ion thrusters.

mcq.q: Compared with chemical rockets, electric propulsion systems provide:
o: Very high specific impulse but low thrust
High thrust and low specific impulse
High thrust and high specific impulse
Low thrust and low specific impulse
mcq.e: Electric thrusters achieve very high exhaust velocities but are limited by available power to low thrust.

mcq.q: For a space-charge-limited plane diode (Child-Langmuir law), the current density varies as:
mcq.e: The Child-Langmuir law gives j ∝ V^(3/2)/d² for space-charge-limited flow.

mcq.q: An arcjet thruster is classified as:
mcq.e: An arcjet heats the propellant with an electric arc and expands it through a nozzle.

IP3151.name: Induction Programme

ex.t: Course details (as given in the official R2021 syllabus)
x: This is a mandatory 2 week programme to be conducted as soon as the students enter the institution.
Normal classes start only after the induction program is over.

The induction programme has been introduced by AICTE with the following objective: “Engineering colleges were established to train graduates well in the branch/department of admission, have a holistic outlook, and have a desire to work for national needs and beyond.
The graduating student must have knowledge and skills in the area of his/her study.
However, he/she must also have a broad understanding of society and relationships.
Character needs to be nurtured as an essential quality by which he/she would understand and fulfill his/her responsibility as an engineer, a citizen and a human being.

Besides the above, several meta-skills and underlying values are needed.” “One will have to work closely with the newly joined students in making them feel comfortable, allow them to explore their academic interests and activities, reduce competition and make them work for excellence, promote bonding within them, build relations between teachers and students, give a broader view of life, and build character.” Hence, the purpose of this programme is to make the students feel comfortable in their new environment, open them up, set a healthy daily routine, create bonding in the batch as well as between faculty and students, develop awareness, sensitivity and understanding of the self, people around them, society at large, and nature.

The following are the activities under the induction program in which the student would be fully engaged throughout the day for the entire duration of the program. (i) Physical Activity This would involve a daily routine of physical activity with games and sports, yoga, gardening, etc. (ii) Creative Arts Every student would choose one skill related to the arts whether visual arts or performing arts.
Examples are painting, sculpture, pottery, music, dance etc.
The student would pursue it everyday for the duration of the program.
These would allow for creative expression.

It would develop a sense of aesthetics and also enhance creativity which would, hopefully, grow into engineering design later. (iii) Universal Human Values This is the anchoring activity of the Induction Programme.

It gets the student to explore oneself and allows one to experience the joy of learning, stand up to peer pressure, make decisions with courage, be aware of relationships with colleagues and supporting stay in the hostel and department, be sensitive to others, etc.
A module in Universal Human Values provides the base.
Methodology of teaching this content is extremely important.
It must not be through do's and don'ts, but get students to explore and think by engaging them in a dialogue.
It is best taught through group discussions and real life activities rather than lecturing.
Discussions would be conducted in small groups of about 20 students with a faculty mentor each.

It would be effective that the faculty mentor assigned is also the faculty advisor for the student for the full duration of the UG programme. (iv) Literary Activity Literary activity would encompass reading, writing and possibly, debating, enacting a play etc. (v) Proficiency Modules This would address some lacunas that students might have, for example, English, computer familiarity etc. (vi) Lectures by Eminent People Motivational lectures by eminent people from all walks of life should be arranged to give the students exposure to people who are socially active or in public life. (vii) Visits to Local Area A couple of visits to the landmarks of the city, or a hospital or orphanage could be organized.

This would familiarize them with the area as well as expose them to the underprivileged. (viii) Familiarization to Dept./Branch & Innovations They should be told about what getting into a branch or department means what role it plays in society, through its technology.

They should also be shown the laboratories, workshops & other facilities. (ix) Department Specific Activities About a week can be spent in introducing activities (games, quizzes, social interactions, small experiments, design thinking etc.) that are relevant to the particular branch of Engineering / Technology / Architecture that can serve as a motivation and kindle interest in building things (become a maker) in that particular field.
This can be conducted in the form of a workshop.
For example, CSE and IT students may be introduced to activities that kindle computational thinking, and get them to build simple games.
ECE students may be introduced to building simple circuits as an extension of their knowledge in Science, and so on.
Students may be asked to build stuff using their knowledge of science.
Induction Programme is totally an activity based programme and therefore there shall be no tests / assessments during this programme.
References: Guide to Induction program from AICTE

CE3512.name: Survey Camp

ex.t: Course details (as given in the official R2021 syllabus)
x: Objectives:
The objective of the survey camp is to enable the students to get practical training in the field work.
Groups of not more than six members in a group will carry out each exercise in survey camp.
At the end of the camp, each student shall have mapped and contoured the area.
The camp record shall include all original field observations, calculations and plots.
Two weeks Survey Camp will be conducted during summer vacation in the following activities: 1.
Traverse – using Theodolite / Total station 2.
Contouring (i).
Radial tachometric contouring - Radial Line at Every 45 Degree and Length not less than 60 Meter on each Radial Line (ii).
Block Level/ By squares of size at least 100 Meter x 100 Meter atleast 20 Meter interval (iii).
L.S & C.S - Road and canal alignment for a Length of not less than 1 Kilo Meter atleast L.S at Every 30M and C.S at every 90 M 3.
Offset of Buildings and Plotting the Location 4.
Sun observation to determine azimuth (guidelines to be given to the students) 5.
Use of GPS to determine latitude and longitude and locate the survey camp location 6.
Traversing using GPS 7.
Curve setting by deflection angle Apart from above students may be given survey exercises in other area also based on site condition to give good exposure on survey.
